drafts.big_idea: Buy verified visitors, not reach. Move Rs 92K out of paid social and creators: in 2025 they cost Rs 274-337 per visitor, and the last Rs 40.2K of paid bought registrations at Rs 200 each against Rs 110 for the first Rs 52.8K. Put it into college, peer and competition channels that convert at Rs 101-154 marginal CPV. Then protect every registration with a measured WhatsApp show-up engine. Result on the same Rs 3L: 2,804 verified visitors base, 3,452 stretch.
drafts.north_star: Unique verified external visitors. A visitor is an external person whose QR check-in is both admitted and verified, deduplicated by stable ID and counted once across both days. Input tree: (registrations by channel x channel show rate) + verified walk-ins. Guardrails: cost per verified visitor (Rs 3,00,000 / visitors) and T-8 reconfirm rate, the leading indicator of show-up. Registrations are an input, never the goal [GRO-01].
city_rationale: Tier-1 by rule: Hyderabad (UA) is an X-class city under the 7th CPC HRA order [mkt HYD-24], and it is cheaper to operate in than Bengaluru, Delhi or Mumbai (Mercer 2024: 202 vs 195/164/136) [mkt HYD-27].
Dense student market: Hyderabad district has 465 colleges (4th in India) and Ranga Reddy 338 (9th) [mkt HYD-04]. Telangana's GER is 46.6 against 30.0 for India [mkt HYD-02].
The pool is clustered, which favours a college grid and bus squads: 107 of 175 Telangana engineering colleges (61%) sit in Hyderabad, Medchal-Malkajgiri and Ranga Reddy [mkt HYD-11].

Tech-heavy audience and a natural sponsor base: 83,622 of 1,16,877 engineering seats (72%) are CSE or allied [mkt HYD-09], and about 515 GCCs operate in the city [mkt HYD-26]. That supports a sponsor-funded hackathon.

Cheap, local media: February is India's cheapest Meta CPM month [PAID-03], Reels CPM runs Rs 45-140 [PAID-01], Hyderabad nano creators charge Rs 3-8K per Reel [INF-03], and Telugu youth media brands are based here (ChaiBisket 903K, Wirally 846K) [MED-10, MED-11].

The market is not the constraint. The stretch target is 3,452 / 5,20,096 = 0.66% of the priority pool, so conversion and cost per visitor are the real limits. The operating limits are known and plannable: HITEX capacity [cal HYD-16], Cyberabad CPPMS permission [cal HYD-26], the 10 pm outdoor sound cut-off [cal HYD-27] and the 11 pm last metro [cal HYD-11].

fest_dates_and_timeline.focus: This weekend comes after the JNTUH II-IV mid-terms (1-6 Feb) [cal HYD-01], the last GATE weekend (20-21 Feb) [cal HYD-07], the I-year mid-terms (3-9 Mar) [cal HYD-02] and Eid (10 Mar) [cal HYD-04]. It comes before Holi (22 Mar) [cal HYD-05] and the second mid-terms (5-10 Apr). Switch to 20-21 Mar if the IPL fixtures (likely Feb) put an SRH home match on 13-14 Mar [cal HYD-09].

Tracking stack: QR pass, partner and ambassador codes, UTMs, WhatsApp BSP; dashboard live by 15 Dec. Recruit 60 ambassadors (non-partner colleges only). Sign the first 20 college MoUs. Pitch competition sponsors. Venue hold and production sponsor (out of scope, but a dependency).

WhatsApp interest list opens. Screen creators. Reach 25 MoUs by 10 Jan. Competition sponsor go/no-go on 15 Jan. Keep pushes quiet during Sankranti (13-17 Jan) [fest HYD-21] and the early-January rival fest window (Elan ran 9-11 Jan in 2026 [mkt HYD-30]).

Registration opens Mon 18 Jan (54 days out). Wave A: 20 partner colleges go live. CTWA pilot flight (Rs 12K) with a geo-lift holdout. Squad-link A/B test. Randomise the 15% reminder holdout. Readout #1 on 31 Jan.
JNTUH mid-terms (1-6 Feb) and GATE (6-7 Feb): no paid flights, partner content only. Readout #2 on Sun 7 Feb decides where the Rs 30K reserve goes.

Release the reserve (8 Feb) to the lowest marginal CPV that is at or below Rs 200. Wave B: 20 more partners. Paid flight 2 (Rs 28K) only if the pilot cleared its thresholds. Competition prelims on weekdays 15-26 Feb (GATE takes the weekends). Ramadan (~9 Feb-10 Mar) means afternoon campus activations. File CPPMS by Fri 12 Feb, at least 4 weeks ahead against the 10/14-day minimum [cal HYD-26]. Acquisition peaks by Sat 27 Feb because identified-to-registered takes a median of 7 days and at most 14 [DS].

Reconfirm-or-release on Fri 5 Mar (Sat 6 Mar is Shivaratri). Backfill the waitlist 5-9 Mar in batches of 100. Close bus manifests 8 Mar. T-2 reminder Thu 11 Mar (after Eid), T-1 Fri 12 Mar. I-year students are messaged only after their mid-terms end on 9 Mar.

Morning-of route and gate message. 4 QR lanes. Live squad check-in leaderboard. Pro-nite 7:30-9:45 pm to respect the 10 pm outdoor sound rule [cal HYD-27]. Shuttle loop to HITEC City metro before the 11 pm last train [cal HYD-11, HYD-15].
Read the holdout and geo-lift tests. Reconcile final CPV by channel and idea. Issue ambassador and squad rewards on verified check-ins only. Write the lessons file for 2028.

Show rate s1 = 1 - (1 - s0) x (1 - 0.20 x 0.85), where 0.85 is the share outside the 15% holdout. Channel lines (2025 spend to 2027 spend: registrations x show rate = visitors): College grid Rs 31K to 80K: 450 x 2.581^0.75 = 916, x 1.10 stall fix = 1,008, net 450 + 558 x 0.8 = 896, x 88.0% = 789. Referrals Rs 19K to 30K: 350 x 1.579^0.70 = 482, net 350 + 132 x 0.8 = 455, x 82.2% = 375. Ambassadors Rs 42K to 40K: 520 x 0.952^0.65 = 504, x 79.2% = 399. Community Rs 16K to 15K: 200 x 0.938^0.60 = 192, x 85.5% = 164. Organic Rs 14K to 10K: 250 x 0.714^0.40 = 219, x 81.7% = 179. Paid social Rs 93K to 40K: 680 x 0.430^0.62 = 403, x 1.20 = 484, net 403 + 81 x 0.8 = 468, x 58.5% = 273. Competitions: 50x3 + 32x4 + 24x6 = 422, x (1 - 0.40) = 253, x 83.4% = 211. Reserve: Rs 30K / Rs 200 = 150 visitors (about 180 registrations). drafts.capacity:
Venue assumption: HITEX Exhibition Centre, Kothaguda/Madhapur (Cyberabad). Hall-4 seats 8,000 theatre-style for the day programme and the Open Area 27,000 for the pro-nite [cal HYD-16]. Venue, production, headliner, metro shuttle and competition prizes are sponsor-funded and outside the Rs 3L marketing budget.

Peak load: day-1 uniques = 69.8% of total (2025: 1,430 / 2,050 [DS]), which is 1,957 base and 2,409 stretch. Peak on site = 65% of day-1 uniques (assumption) = 1,272 / 1,566 external visitors, plus about 1,500 non-counted people (organising students, volunteers, artists, crew, vendors; assumption). That gives a peak of about 2,772 base and 3,066 stretch.

Gates: peak-hour arrivals are 17.6% of day uniques (2025: 251 of 1,430 in the 11:00 hour), so 344 base and 424 stretch per hour. Four QR lanes at about 450 scans/hour each give 1,800/hour, 4x headroom. Target under 3% manual admissions (2025: 9.4%).

Permission sizing: apply on Cyberabad CPPMS for 7,000 peak concurrent, about 2.3x the modelled stretch peak. General entry stays free and non-ticketed (10-day rule; 14 days if ticketed). File by 12 Feb [cal HYD-26]. Hard caps keep even the worst case inside the permit: passes capped at 4,500 (stretch needs 4,014) and walk-ins at 300/day. Worst case, all 4,500 + 300 + 1,500 arrive on day 1 = 6,300, which is under 7,000. This guards against the Malla Reddy failure (permission for about 7,000, about 20,000 turned up [fest HYD-13]) and the Mood Indigo gate crush [fest NAT-01].

Night limits: outdoor sound ends at 10 pm [cal HYD-27], so the pro-nite runs 7:30-9:45 pm. HITEX is 2.6 km from HITEC City metro [cal HYD-15] and the last train leaves at 11 pm [cal HYD-11], so a shuttle loop runs 9:45-10:45 pm. We will also ask HMRL for late trains, citing the NYE and IPL precedents [cal HYD-12]. Afternoon highs near 35 C in March [cal HYD-10] push crowd-heavy programming to the evening.

The stretch fits the same permit. The binding constraints are budget and team bandwidth, not capacity.

framework.name: ICE (Impact, Confidence, Ease; Sean Ellis [GRO-03]) with anchored scales, gated by a marginal-CPV rule
framework.how_scored: Each idea is scored 1-10 on three anchored scales, and ICE = (I + C + E) / 3. Impact = midpoint of base and stretch incremental verified visitors / 45, so 10 means about 450 visitors. Confidence = evidence tier: 9 = RCT plus own data, 8 = own 2025 channel data or RCTs from other domains, 6 = own data plus vendor benchmarks, 4 = external analogues only. Ease = cash, owner-hours and external dependencies: 9 = Rs 20K or less, self-serve, one owner; 5 = many external sign-offs; 4 = needs a sponsor plus multi-team ops. Scores: #1 Grid (10 + 8 + 5) / 3 = 7.7; #2 Show-up engine (4 + 8 + 9) / 3 = 7.0; #3 Peer loop (3 + 7 + 7) / 3 = 5.7; #4 Paid rebuild (2 + 6 + 8) / 3 = 5.3; #5 Compete (5 + 4 + 4) / 3 = 4.3. The gate applies to every idea on 'projected CPV' (spend / registrations x the channel's show prior, recalibrated by reconfirm rate after 5 Mar): Rs 120 or less = scale, Rs 120-200 = hold, Rs 200-250 = change, above Rs 250 for 2 consecutive weeks = stop (2025 paid was Rs 274). Allocation rule: fill peer channels up to their operational caps, because they have the lowest marginal CPV (Rs 114-154). Paid gets the remainder as a gated test. The reserve chases the lowest marginal CPV.

ideas.name: College Partnership Grid + college-bus squads
ideas.concept: Scale 2025's best channel from Rs 31K to Rs 80K and run it as an always-on grid of 40 partner colleges: 30 engineering colleges across Hyderabad, Medchal-Malkajgiri and Ranga Reddy, plus 10 large OU-area degree and women's colleges. Each MoU gives the college: a partner code and pass quota; a club co-hosted pre-event on campus (IEEE branch, E-cell or cultural club); a showcase slot at the fest; and a 'college-bus squad', where the college sends its own bus on the Saturday for a 40-seat squad and we pay the diesel and driver top-up. A weekly cadence SLA means no partner goes dark for more than 7 days.
ideas.why_it_works: Own data [DS]: partnerships had the best funnel of any channel: 90.0% identified-to-registered, 85.6% registered-to-visited, 91.7% confirmed-to-visited, a 4.0% cancel rate and Rs 81 CPV. The channel was idle for about 3 weeks (weekly regs 21, 8, 0 in weeks 8-10; spend postings skip 4-28 Feb), so it was under-invested, not saturated. In Hyderabad, 61% of engineering colleges sit in 3 districts [mkt HYD-11]. Buses remove the distance cost (2-3 pp of turnout per extra mile [SHOW-17]) and make attendance a visible group act (+8.1 pp [SHOW-15]); 70% of Gen Z attend events in groups [MED-25].
ideas.contribution_math: Response curve: 450 x (Rs 80K / Rs 31K)^0.75 = 916 registrations. The x1.10 stall fix is measured: 2025 weeks 8-10 delivered 29 regs against 78 at the weeks 6-7 run-rate of 26/week, i.e. 49 lost = 10.9% of 450. So 916 x 1.10 = 1,008 gross. A 20% cannibalisation haircut on the increment gives 450 + 558 x 0.8 = 896 net registrations. Credited at the 2025 show rate: (896 - 450) x 85.6% = +382. Stretch: x1.25 (stall fix + bus squads) gives 1,145 gross, 1,006 net, +476. Unit economics: avg CPV Rs 101, marginal Rs 135 (Rs 101 / beta 0.75). New cash +Rs 49K / 382 = Rs 128 per incremental visitor. Operating target: 896 / 40 partners = 22.4 each, about 4.5 per partner per selling week over 5 weeks.
ideas.resources: Owner: partnerships lead, with 8 volunteers (one per 5 colleges). 40 faculty coordinators and club leads (in kind). Rs 40K partner kits and club events, Rs 35K bus top-ups (10 bus-days x Rs 3,500, assumption), Rs 5K partner-code QR standees.
ideas.timeline: MoUs 1 Dec-10 Jan (25 by 10 Jan, 40 by 31 Jan). Wave A: 20 partners live Mon 18 Jan. Wave B: 20 partners live Mon 8 Feb, after mid-terms. Club pre-events 18-31 Jan and 8-27 Feb. Bus booking 15 Feb-8 Mar; buses run 13-14 Mar.
ideas.test_design: The staggered rollout doubles as a natural experiment: Wave A vs Wave B partners, matched on size and district, compared on registrations per partner-week. Bus test: 10 bus partners vs 10 size-matched no-bus partners, compared on registered-to-visited (expect at least 5 pp). Unique partner codes give clean attribution.

ideas.framework_scores: ICE: Impact 10 (midpoint 429 / 45 = 9.5), Confidence 8 (own 2025 data; stall measured; beta 0.75 assumed), Ease 5 (40 external sign-offs plus bus logistics in about 6 weeks), giving 7.7. Rank 1: double down.
ideas.dependencies_risks_overlap: Dependencies: principal and faculty sign-off before winter breaks; partner buses free on a Saturday (assumption); 6 campuses reused as #5 prelim hosts. Risks: partners going dark (the 2025 stall); I-year mid-terms 3-9 Mar [cal HYD-02]; Ramadan evenings (~9 Feb-10 Mar [cal HYD-04]), so activations run in the afternoon. Overlap: ambassadors (#3) may operate only in non-partner colleges. Partner codes outrank referral, ambassador and paid codes in attribution (only competition codes rank higher). The 20% haircut covers students who would have arrived through another route.
ideas.critical_variables: Active partners per week; registrations per active partner-week (model 4.5); partner CPR; bus seat fill; partner registrants' reconfirm rate.
ideas.early_success_signal: At least 25 MoUs by 10 Jan; at least 18 of Wave A's 20 active in the week of 18 Jan; at least 4.5 registrations per partner-week by 14 Feb; at least 70% of bus seats booked by 1 Mar.
ideas.early_failure_signal: Fewer than 15 MoUs by 10 Jan; any partner at zero registrations for 7 days (the 2025 week-8 pattern); under 2 registrations per partner-week in the first two selling weeks.
ideas.scale_threshold: Projected CPV at or below Rs 120 and at least 5 registrations per partner-week at the 8 Feb readout: draw Rs 15-30K from the reserve to add 10 partners and 5 buses.
ideas.change_threshold: 2-4.5 registrations per partner-week, or projected CPV Rs 120-200: swap the activation format (a club co-hosted mini-event instead of posters) and move volunteer hours to top-quartile partners.
ideas.stop_threshold: A partner under 1 registration/week for 2 consecutive weeks is dropped and its campus handed to ambassadors. A bus with fewer than 25 seats booked by 8 Mar is cancelled and replaced with metro-route instructions. Grid projected CPV above Rs 250 for 2 weeks freezes new partner sign-ups.
ideas.action_on_change: Monday review: re-rank partners by registrations per partner-week. A dark partner gets a call within 24 hours and a replacement club lead. Money moves between partners within 48 hours, and reserve draws require the 8 Feb readout.
ideas.dashboard_ai_support: Dashboard: partner leaderboard showing regs, reconfirms, bus fill and projected visitors (regs x the 85.6% prior until T-8, then reconfirm-calibrated). A 'dark partner' alert fires at 7 days of zero regs; it would have caught the 2025 stall in week 8. AI copilot: drafts each partner's weekly nudge from its own numbers, ranks which partner should get the next bus (highest projected show lift per Rs 3,500), and answers 'which 5 partners should we drop?'. Nothing is sent or reallocated without human approval (toolApproval [SDK-05]), and only aggregated data reaches the model [GEM-06].

ideas.name: 'Reserved-for-you' WhatsApp show-up engine
ideas.concept: Turn each registration into a held seat and nudge it to the gate. (1) Registration ends with a WhatsApp QR pass worded 'your spot is reserved'. (2) A plan-making step: which day, which metro station or college bus, and who you are coming with. (3) No limbo: registrations auto-confirm, and released spots backfill the waitlist. (4) Utility-template cadence: confirmation; reconfirm-or-release on Fri 5 Mar (T-8); T-2 on Thu 11 Mar; T-1 on Fri 12 Mar; morning-of route and gate message. (5) Win-back for cancellations. A 15% squad-level holdout gets the pass only.
ideas.why_it_works: Own data [DS]: confirmed registrants showed at 77%; cancelled, waitlisted and limbo registrants at 0%. 117 registrants (4.2%) leaked through the waitlist or never confirmed. Win-back worked (36 of 219 cancellations reconfirmed). The single nurture email had no lift (69.0% vs 68.7%) and 12.7% of recipients opted out. Evidence: text reminders cut no-shows by 25% (RR 0.75) [SHOW-09]; 3-day plus 1-day reminders beat either alone [SHOW-10]; 'reserved for you' ownership wording performed best [SHOW-13]; plan-making adds 4.1 pp [SHOW-14]. 2025's 31.25% registrant no-show was worse than the ~24% median for large free events [SHOW-02]. A utility message costs about Rs 0.24 all-in [WA-01, WA-04].
ideas.contribution_math: Base: a 20% relative cut in no-shows on the 85% treated share (effective 17%), so s1 = 1 - (1 - s0) x 0.83 per channel (grid 85.6% to 88.0%; paid 50% to 58.5%). Credit = sum of 2027 registrations x (s1 - s0) = 133.7 (channels) + 8.6 (competitions) = +142. Bottom-up check on the 20%: the leak fix is about 2.6 pp (117 x 80% recovered x 77%), and reminders at RR 0.85 on confirmed no-shows (the RCT found 0.75) add about 3.1 pp. That is 5.7 of 31.25 pp, or 18%. Stretch: the full RCT effect plus plan-making = 30% x 85% = 25.5%, giving +251. The holdout costs 25 visitors in base, the price of proof. Rs 20,000 / 142 = Rs 141 per incremental visitor (Rs 80 in stretch).
ideas.resources: Owner: growth and analytics lead (the candidate), plus 1 volunteer on the WhatsApp inbox. BSP (Gupshup/Interakt class) Rs 10,000 (Rs 2,500/month x 4 [WA-04]); about 20,400 utility messages (3,403 x 6) x Rs 0.24 = Rs 4,900; SMS fallback Rs 2,000 [SMS-02]; QR and printing Rs 3,100. Registration and QR check-in run on a free plan for free events [SHOW-24].
ideas.timeline: Templates approved and flow built by 10 Jan. Live with registration on 18 Jan. Reconfirm-or-release Fri 5 Mar (Sat 6 Mar is Shivaratri). Waitlist backfill 5-9 Mar. T-2 Thu 11 Mar (after Eid). T-1 Fri 12 Mar. Morning-of messages 13-14 Mar. Holdout readout 20 Mar.
ideas.test_design: Randomise 15% of registration groups to pass-only. Randomising at squad level keeps friends in the same arm, which avoids spillover. Pre-registered primary metric: verified check-in. A one-sided test at alpha 0.05 with 80% power detects a gap of 5.2 pp or more with about 510 holdout vs 2,890 treated (sample-size method [GRO-04]). Early proxy on the same split: T-8 reconfirm rate. Inside the treatment arm, A/B the T-1 copy: ownership ('your seat is held') vs loss-framed with travel time [SHOW-11, SHOW-12].
kpis: WhatsApp opt-in at registration: at least 90%
Template delivery at least 95%; opt-out/block under 3%
Plan completion (day + route + squad): at least 60%
T-8 reconfirm: treated at least 75% and at least 8 pp above holdout
Spots released and backfilled (count)
Event day: treated vs holdout show gap of at least 5 pp
ideas.framework_scores: ICE: Impact 4 (midpoint 196 / 45 = 4.4), Confidence 8 (RCTs from other domains plus own leak data; transfer to fests is the uncertainty), Ease 9 (Rs 20K, off-the-shelf tools, one owner), giving 7.0. Rank 2: double down, since it is the cheapest insurance on every other idea.
ideas.dependencies_risks_overlap: Dependencies: opt-in captured at registration; Meta template approval; messages classed as utility (marketing costs 7.5x more at Rs 0.8631 [WA-01]). Risks: fatigue and blocks; Eid timing; the holdout costs about 25 visitors. Overlap: the engine acts on registrations generated by every other idea, so it is credited only with the show-rate uplift (s1 - s0) on 2027 registrants and never with registrations. No separate 'lead-time' lift is added: 2025's weaker 31-60-day cohort (72.1% vs about 81%) coincides with the paid-social peak (weeks 6-9 were 41-68 days out), so that gap is channel mix and is already captured.
ideas.critical_variables: Opt-in rate; delivery rate; T-8 reconfirm rate (treated vs holdout); plan-completion rate; opt-out/block rate; release-to-backfill count.
ideas.early_success_signal: By 5-6 Mar: treated reconfirm at least 75% and at least 8 pp above holdout; plan completion at least 60%; opt-out under 3% (against 12.7% for 2025's email).
ideas.early_failure_signal: Reconfirm gap under 3 pp; delivery under 90%; opt-out/block above 5% on any send; opt-in at registration under 70%.
ideas.scale_threshold: Reconfirm gap of 8 pp or more: add day-1 'your squad is here' live nudges and a day-2 nudge to day-1 no-shows, and move the plan-making prompt into the squad-share step (#3).
ideas.change_threshold: Gap of 3-8 pp: switch T-1 copy to the winning A/B arm, add the SMS fallback for non-opt-ins, and move T-2 to T-3.
ideas.stop_threshold: Opt-out/block above 5% on 2 consecutive sends: cut to the two best-evidenced touches (3-day and 1-day [SHOW-10]). Retire any template with a block rate above 2%.
ideas.action_on_change: Re-send only to non-responders. Released seats go to the waitlist in batches of 100 with a 24-hour claim window. Reconfirm rates by channel replace the 2025 show priors in the visitor forecast and the projected-CPV gate.
ideas.dashboard_ai_support: Dashboard show-up panel: reconfirm rate by channel, college and arm; projected visitors (reconfirmed x arm-specific show rate); waitlist and release counter; holdout gap with a confidence interval. AI copilot: drafts message variants within template rules, flags colleges with reconfirm under 60% to the partnership owner, and answers 'if reconfirm holds at X%, how many visitors on Saturday?'. Every send needs human approval (toolApproval [SDK-05]); no PII goes to the free-tier model [GEM-06].

ideas.name: Verified-attendance peer loop (squad pass + ambassador ladder)
ideas.concept: One loop with two tiers, paid only on verified check-ins. Every registrant's WhatsApp pass carries a squad link: a squad of 4 or more that all check in gets fast-lane entry, a pro-nite front zone and a merch draw. 60 campus ambassadors in non-partner colleges climb a ladder by their recruits' verified check-ins: 10 = certificate, 25 = T-shirt plus a guest pass, 50 = pro-nite pit plus a recommendation letter, top 10 = recognition on stage. The tier design follows IIT Ropar and Techfest [CA-01, fest NAT-05].
ideas.why_it_works: Own data [DS]: referrals were the cheapest channel (Rs 69 CPV, 78.6% show) and ambassadors the largest single source (390 visitors, Rs 108). Attendance is a group decision: 70% of Indian Gen Z attend with friends [MED-25], 59% would skip if they knew no one [SHOW-16], and visible group attendance lifts turnout by 8.1 pp [SHOW-15]. Paying on check-ins instead of sign-ups removes the incentive for fake or low-intent registrations and makes ambassadors chase show-up.
ideas.contribution_math: Referrals: 350 x (Rs 30K / Rs 19K)^0.70 = 482; with a 20% haircut on the increment, 455 net; (455 - 350) x 78.6% = +83. Ambassadors: 520 x (Rs 40K / Rs 42K)^0.65 = 504; (504 - 520) x 75.0% = -12. Base = +71. Stretch: referrals x1.25 (squad pass) = 602 gross, 552 net, +158.7; ambassadors x1.15 (ladder) = 579 gross, 567 net, +35.6; total +194. Loop check: referred registrations per 100 non-referral registrants = 455 / 2,948 = 15.4 in base (2025: 350 / 2,450 = 14.3; stretch 552 / 3,462 = 15.9). Cash is +Rs 9K vs 2025 (Rs 61K to Rs 70K), so Rs 127 per incremental visitor. Average CPV: referrals Rs 80, ambassadors Rs 100.
ideas.resources: Owner: community lead. 60 ambassadors recruited 1-20 Dec in non-partner colleges. Rs 40K for ladder rewards, Rs 30K for squad-completion merch. Fast-lane and front-zone access are zero-cash production assets.
ideas.timeline: Recruit 1-20 Dec. Onboarding and codes 4-10 Jan. Squad links live with registration on 18 Jan. Weekly leaderboard (paused 1-7 Feb). Rewards issued 15-25 Mar after check-in reconciliation.
ideas.test_design: A/B at registration, 50/50 by registration ID: squad link with a check-in reward vs a plain share link. Metrics: referred registrations per 100 registrants and the show rate of referred registrants. In parallel, ladder vs flat certificate in two matched college clusters for the first 3 weeks.
kpis: Squad-link share rate within 48 hours of registering: at least 25%
Referred registrations per 100 non-referral registrants: at least 15.4
Squad completion (3 or more registered): at least 40% of squads started
Ambassador activation (5 or more regs in the first 14 days): at least 60%
Duplicate or fake recruits per ambassador: under 5%
Projected referral CPV: Rs 100 or less
ideas.framework_scores: ICE: Impact 3 (midpoint 133 / 45 = 2.9), Confidence 7 (own 2025 data for both channels; the squad uplift is an external-evidence assumption), Ease 7 (one owner plus 60 ambassadors; needs clean dedupe), giving 5.7. Rank 3: restructure, not expand.
ideas.dependencies_risks_overlap: Depends on #2's WhatsApp pass, which is the share moment, and on person-level dedupe for an honest leaderboard. Risks: ambassador fraud, inactive ambassadors (CA programmes typically over-recruit), and reward cost if squads over-perform (merch capped at Rs 30K). Overlap: ambassadors are barred from partner colleges; referral links lose attribution to partner and competition codes; 20% haircut on increments.
ideas.critical_variables: Share rate; referred registrations per 100 registrants; squad completion; ambassador activation; recruits' reconfirm rate; duplicate rate.
ideas.early_success_signal: By 31 Jan: share rate at least 25% and at least 60% of ambassadors activated. By 14 Feb: at least 15 referred registrations per 100 non-referral registrants.
ideas.early_failure_signal: Share rate under 10%; ambassador activation under 40% at day 14; more than 10% of any ambassador's recruits failing OTP or dedupe.
ideas.scale_threshold: Projected referral CPV at or below Rs 100 and squad completion at least 40%: add a 6+ squad tier funded from the reserve (up to Rs 10K).
ideas.change_threshold: Share rate 10-25%: move the share prompt into the plan-making 'who are you coming with?' step, and switch the reward to the zero-cash pro-nite front zone.
ideas.stop_threshold: An ambassador with more than 10% duplicate or fake recruits is disqualified. An ambassador inactive at day 14 is replaced. If projected peer CPV stays above Rs 250 for 2 weeks, freeze merch spend and keep only the zero-cash perks.
ideas.action_on_change: Weekly leaderboard reset each Monday. The bottom quartile of ambassadors gets a 1:1 call or is replaced. Merch budget shifts toward squads, which complete at higher rates than individual referrals.
ideas.dashboard_ai_support: Leaderboard ranked by projected verified check-ins (reconfirms before the event, actual scans on the day); a squad graph; anomaly flags for same device, sequential phone numbers or burst sign-ups. AI copilot: drafts each ambassador's nudge showing their gap to the next tier, and explains flagged anomalies for human review. It cannot disqualify anyone without approval.

ideas.name: Paid rebuilt as Click-to-WhatsApp Reels + Telugu nano creators, behind a CPV kill switch
ideas.concept: Cut paid social plus creators from Rs 1,52,000 to Rs 60,000 and rebuild what remains. (a) Rs 40K for Meta Reels and Stories only: Click-to-WhatsApp ads geo-fenced to the three metro districts and partner-college areas, retargeting people who engaged with partner or ambassador content. Two flights: a pilot 18-31 Jan (Rs 12K) and a scale flight 8-27 Feb (Rs 28K, only if the pilot clears its gate), with weekly creative rotation. (b) Rs 20K for 4-5 Hyderabad Telugu nano creators at Rs 3-8K per Reel [INF-03], screened for at least 3% engagement and audience authenticity, with their content reused as ad creative. Barter (passes, stage time) offered to ChaiBisket and Wirally is unmodelled upside.
ideas.why_it_works: Own data [DS]: paid social took 33.9% of spend for 16.6% of visitors (Rs 274 CPV, 50% show, 12.2% opt-out) and showed clear diminishing returns. Its first Rs 52.8K bought registrations at Rs 110 each, the last Rs 40.2K at Rs 200 each, and weekly regs fell from 105 to 35 at the same Rs 14,400 in week 10. Cutting back to the efficient part of the curve keeps most of the volume. Reels CPM is Rs 45-140 against Rs 150-350 for Feed [PAID-01]. A CTWA chat opens a free 7-day messaging window [WA-03], so each lead drops straight into #2's flow. February is India's cheapest CPM month [PAID-03]. Regional micro creators get 2-3x the engagement at about one-tenth the cost [INF-04].
ideas.contribution_math: The plain shrink is booked in the -242 reallocation line. Paid: 680 x (40/93)^0.62 = 403; beta 0.62 is implied by 2025's own weekly data. Creators: 350 x (20/59)^0.5 = 204. Loss = (403 - 680) x 50% + (204 - 350) x 50% = -211.5 visitors. This idea is credited only with its structural gain. Base: x1.20 registrations per rupee gives 484 paid and 245 creator registrations gross; after the 20% haircut, 468 and 236 net; (64.6 + 32.6) x 50% = about +48. Stretch: x1.50 gives 564 and 285 net, +121. Net vs 2025: -211.5 + 48 = -163 visitors while freeing Rs 92,000, which is Rs 564 saved per visitor given up. The same Rs 92K buys about 680 visitors at the grid's Rs 135 marginal CPV. Paid CPR in base: Rs 86 (2025: Rs 137).
ideas.resources: Owner: growth and analytics lead (shared with #2), with the content lead writing creator briefs. Meta Ads Manager with CTWA. 4-5 nano creators. Phone-shot Reels produced in-house.
ideas.timeline: Creator screening 4-15 Jan. Pilot flight 18-31 Jan (Rs 12K plus 2 creators). No paid 1-7 Feb (mid-terms, GATE). Gate decision 7 Feb. Scale flight 8-27 Feb (Rs 28K plus 2-3 creators) only if the pilot passed. After 27 Feb, only retargeting of registrants who have not reconfirmed (up to Rs 2K).
ideas.test_design: Geo-lift holdout in the pilot: run CTWA in two of the three metro districts and keep the third dark for 2 weeks, then compare registrations per 1,000 engineering seats. This is needed because first-touch attribution overstates paid. Creative A/B: Telugu vs English, Reels vs Stories. Each creator gets a unique code.
kpis: Reels CPM at or below Rs 140; cost per WhatsApp conversation
CTWA conversation-to-registration: at least 25% (2025 paid landing-to-start was 21.7%)
Paid CPR at or below Rs 86; creator CPR at or below Rs 85
Paid registrants' T-8 reconfirm: at least 65% (2025 paid show was 50%)
Weekly CTR decay under 30%; frequency 3 or less
Projected weekly CPV at or below Rs 200
ideas.framework_scores: ICE: Impact 2 (midpoint 85 / 45 = 1.9; its real value is the Rs 92K it releases), Confidence 6 (own-data beta 0.62 plus vendor CPM benchmarks), Ease 8 (self-serve, one owner), giving 5.3. Rank 4: shrink and fix.
ideas.dependencies_risks_overlap: Depends on #2 (CTWA leads land in the WhatsApp flow) and on #1 and #3 content to build retargeting pools. Risks: creative fatigue (the 2025 week-10 collapse); low-intent leads (2025 paid showed 50% with 12.2% opt-out); fake creator audiences (1 in 4 profiles fail an authenticity screen [INF-04]); an Instagram ad audience that is about 70% male [MED-01], so female-led creators are preferred. Overlap: retargeted people were often first touched by peers, and first-touch precedence credits them to the peer channel. The 20% haircut applies to the structural gain, and the geo-lift test measures true incrementality.
ideas.critical_variables: Reels CPM; CTR decay; cost per CTWA conversation; CPR; paid registrants' reconfirm rate; creator registrations per Rs 1,000.
ideas.early_success_signal: Pilot (18-31 Jan): CPR at or below Rs 86; paid registrants' plan completion or reconfirm at least 65%; positive geo-lift; creators delivering at least 1 registration per Rs 1,000.
ideas.early_failure_signal: Pilot CPR above Rs 130; opt-out above 8%; geo-lift indistinguishable from zero.
ideas.scale_threshold: Projected CPV at or below Rs 120 on 7 Feb: run flight 2 at the full Rs 28K plus up to Rs 15K from the reserve.
ideas.change_threshold: Projected CPV Rs 120-250, or CTR down more than 30% week on week: rotate creative, shift from the cold geo-fence to retargeting engagers, and swap out the weakest creator.
ideas.stop_threshold: Projected weekly CPV above Rs 250 for 2 consecutive weeks (2025 actual: Rs 274): pause and return the remainder to the reserve. A creator below 1 registration per Rs 1,000 gets no second post.
ideas.action_on_change: Budget moves within 2 days of a threshold being crossed. Every rupee pulled goes to the reserve, which only the lowest-marginal-CPV idea can draw on.
ideas.dashboard_ai_support: Daily CPR and projected CPV (CPR / reconfirm-calibrated show rate) by ad set and creator; a CTR-decay fatigue alert; the geo-lift chart. AI copilot: proposes budget shifts with their expected visitor impact (change in Rs / marginal CPV). A human approves before any spend changes [SDK-05].

ideas.name: Compete-to-attend: sponsor-funded team competitions
ideas.concept: Give people a reason to come as a team. Three sponsor-funded tracks, where registering a team issues a fest pass to every member: a 24-hour AI hackathon with GCC sponsors (base 50 teams x 3), an inter-college BGMI/esports cup (32 squads x 4), and cultural crew battles with weekday prelims on 6 partner campuses (24 crews x 6). Listed on Unstop. Prizes of Rs 2-3L come from sponsors. Only external participants who check in count.
ideas.why_it_works: 72% of Telangana engineering seats are CSE or allied [mkt HYD-09], and about 515 GCCs give a natural hackathon sponsor base [mkt HYD-26]. Prize pools reliably pull teams in Hyderabad (Infinium Rs 12.2L [fest HYD-06]; Elan Rs 16L [fest HYD-02]), and BGMI lobbies drew crowds at Hyderabad Comic Con [fest HYD-17]. Unstop reaches 32M+ students [SHOW-28]. Teams are pre-formed squads with peer accountability; in 2025, engaged registrants (those who submitted a question) showed at 79.4% vs 68.0% [DS].
ideas.contribution_math: Base: 50 x 3 + 32 x 4 + 24 x 6 = 422 participant registrations. A 40% overlap haircut (many participants come from partner colleges and ambassador networks) leaves 253 net; x 80% show = +203. The show-up engine adds 9 more on top, booked under #2. Stretch: 70 x 3 + 48 x 4 + 32 x 6 = 594, 356 net, x 80% = +285. Cash cost: Rs 15K / 203 = Rs 74 per visitor. Fully loaded with Rs 2.5L of sponsor prizes it is about Rs 1,305 per visitor, so the idea only makes sense if sponsors pay.
ideas.resources: Owner: competitions and content lead. 6 partner campuses host prelims (from #1). Judges and mentors from IIT-H, IIIT-H and BITS-H as credibility partners. Rs 15K for Unstop promotion and prelim logistics. The prize pool is sponsor-funded and out of scope.
ideas.timeline: Sponsor pitch 1 Dec-15 Jan, with a go/no-go on 15 Jan. Unstop listings 18 Jan. Weekday prelims 15-26 Feb (GATE takes the weekends). Registrations close 27 Feb. Finals 13-14 Mar.
ideas.test_design: The slot-fill gates are pre-registered decision points. Incrementality check: compare check-in rate and first-time-visitor share for competitors vs non-competitor registrants from the same colleges. A one-question check-in survey ('would you have come without the competition?') serves only as a sanity check on the 40% haircut.
kpis: Sponsor signed by 15 Jan (Rs 2-3L pool)
Slot fill vs plan: 50 / 32 / 24 teams
Team completion (every member holds a pass): at least 90%
Prelim turnout: at least 70%
Participant check-in rate: at least 80%
Cash CPV: Rs 74 or less
ideas.framework_scores: ICE: Impact 5 (midpoint 244 / 45 = 5.4), Confidence 4 (no 2025 data; external analogues only), Ease 4 (needs a sponsor, judges and ops), giving 4.3. Rank 5: an option bet gated by the sponsor.
ideas.dependencies_risks_overlap: Depends on sponsor cash, #1 partner campuses for prelims, and venue space for a 24-hour hackathon (production). Risks: no sponsor; flagship-campus teams prioritising their own fests; esports conduct rules. Overlap is the highest of any idea, hence the 40% haircut. Competition codes take attribution precedence, so a participant is never also credited to the grid or the peer loop.
ideas.critical_variables: Sponsor signing date; slot fill by track; team completion; prelim turnout; participant check-in rate.
ideas.early_success_signal: Sponsor signed by 15 Jan; at least 60% of base slots filled by 14 Feb (30 / 19 / 14); prelim turnout at least 70%.
ideas.early_failure_signal: No sponsor by 15 Jan; under 30% of slots filled by 14 Feb.
ideas.scale_threshold: At least 90% of slots filled by 14 Feb: open 20% more slots and add a supporter pass per team, within the 4,500 pass cap.
ideas.change_threshold: One track under 30% while others fill: move promotion to the faster-filling track and shorten the hackathon to 12 hours.
ideas.stop_threshold: No sponsor by 15 Jan: drop the hackathon and keep esports and cultural tracks with in-kind prizes. All tracks under 30% on 14 Feb: stop and move the Rs 15K to the grid (about 110 visitors at Rs 135 marginal).
ideas.action_on_change: The track owner reallocates promotion weekly. The 15 Jan and 14 Feb gates are fixed in advance, so sunk-cost reasoning cannot keep a failing track alive.
ideas.dashboard_ai_support: Slot-fill tracker per track against the gates, plus a list of incomplete teams. AI copilot: drafts the sponsor's ROI one-pager from live, aggregated registration counts, and nudges captains of incomplete teams after human approval.

drafts.overlap_adjustment:
Four guards keep the five contributions from double counting.

(1) The North Star counts unique stable IDs once across both days, so the total itself cannot double count.

(2) Every registrant is attributed to exactly one source, by precedence: competition team code, then partner-college code, then squad/referral link, then ambassador code, then paid/creator UTM, then organic. Ambassadors may operate only in non-partner colleges.

(3) The decomposition is exact. Acquisition ideas are credited only with net new registrations, valued at the 2025 channel show rate: (R1 - R0) x s0. The show-up engine is credited only with the uplift on all 2027 registrants: R1 x (s1 - s0), net of the 15% holdout. Shrinking paid, creators, organic and community is booked as a separate negative line (-242). The paid rebuild is credited only with its gain above that plain shrink.

(4) Every positive acquisition increment is cut by a cannibalisation haircut: 20% for the grid, the peer loop and the paid gain, 40% for competitions. A separate 'lead-time' lift is deliberately not added, because 2025's weak 31-60-day cohort coincides with the paid-social peak.

Base: 2,050 - 242 + 382 (#1 grid) + 142 (#2 engine) + 71 (#3 peer) + 48 (#4 paid gain) + 203 (#5 compete) + 150 (reserve) + 0 (walk-ins) = 2,804.

Stretch: 2,050 - 242 + 476 + 251 + 194 + 121 + 285 + 231 + 86 = 3,452.

Sensitivity: raising the haircuts to 30% and 50% lowers base by 102.

deprioritized.idea: Broad paid prospecting on Feed placements, and macro or national influencers
deprioritized.reason: 2025 paid cost Rs 274 per visitor with 50% show and 12.2% opt-out; creators cost Rs 337 [DS]. One macro Reel costs Rs 2-12L [INF-01], which would consume the whole budget. Even after the cut, paid's marginal CPV in the model (Rs 236) is the highest of any line. Cut from Rs 1,52,000 to Rs 60,000.

deprioritized.idea: Generic nurture email blasts
deprioritized.reason: Zero measured lift (69.0% vs 68.7% show) and 12.7% of recipients opted out [DS]. Indian M&E broadcast email gets 17% open and 2.2% CTOR [EMAIL-01]. Replaced by triggered WhatsApp (#2).

deprioritized.idea: Paid stalls or sponsorships at other colleges' fests
deprioritized.reason: Rs 15K-2L each [PART-01]. This buys reach, not verified visitors, and is not trackable to check-in. Partnerships are done in kind through the grid instead.

deprioritized.idea: Paid general entry, or a refundable deposit for everyone
deprioritized.reason: Free entry is the Hyderabad norm [fest landscape], so charging would cut reach. Within the same event, payers show only 2-4 pp more often [SHOW-04]. The deposit evidence is a single US anecdote [SHOW-08]. Ticketing also changes the permission class to the Commissioner of Police with 14 days' notice [cal HYD-26]. Kept only as a contingency test if the T-8 reconfirm rate falls below 55%.

deprioritized.idea: Young IT/GCC professionals as an audience segment
deprioritized.reason: There is no 2025 conversion data to price them, they need different channels, and evening slots collide with the 10 pm sound limit and the 11 pm metro. GCCs are used as hackathon sponsors instead.

deprioritized.idea: Flagship residential campuses as volume sources
deprioritized.reason: Only about 19,400 students across IIT-H, BITS-H, UoH, IIIT-H and ISB. They are peripheral, run their own large fests and recycle the same acts. They are used as credibility partners (judges, mentors) only.

deprioritized.idea: A bigger headliner paid from the marketing budget
deprioritized.reason: It is a production cost, not marketing. It also carries crowd-safety risk (Malla Reddy: about 7,000 permitted, about 20,000 arrived [fest HYD-13]), and acts recycle across Hyderabad fests within weeks [fest HYD-09]. No headliner uplift is modelled even in stretch.

deprioritized.idea: Scaling organic search and SEO
deprioritized.reason: It mostly captures demand that other channels create. Its elasticity is low (beta 0.4) and first-touch credit overstates its incrementality. Held at Rs 10K.

assumptions.assumption: 2025 CampusFest channel rates transfer to Hyderabad 2027
assumptions.value: Identified-to-registered, registered-to-visited and CPR by channel as in [DS]
assumptions.basis: Own data is the only channel-level evidence; the 2025 city is unspecified. Hyderabad's priority pool (5.2 lakh) is about 150x the target, so market depth is not the limit.
assumptions.sensitivity: All CPRs 15% worse: base -284 (to 2,520). Combined with failed competitions and an unspent reserve, the floor is 2,158, still above 2,050.

assumptions.value: Grid 0.75, referrals 0.70, ambassadors 0.65, community 0.60, organic 0.40, paid social 0.62, creators 0.50
assumptions.basis: Paid social's 0.62 is implied by 2025 weekly data (first Rs 52.8K gave 479 regs at Rs 110; the next Rs 40.2K gave 201 at Rs 200). The others are assumptions: peer channels scale with headcount, and organic is captured demand. Creators' weekly data shows lagged response, so their beta is untested.
assumptions.sensitivity: Grid beta 0.5 instead of 0.75: base -150.

assumptions.value: x1.10 base, x1.25 stretch
assumptions.basis: 2025 weeks 8-10 delivered 29 regs against 78 at the weeks 6-7 run-rate, so 49 lost = 10.9% of 450 [DS]. The stretch adds bus squads [SHOW-17, SHOW-15].
assumptions.sensitivity: No stall fix: base -65.

assumptions.value: 20% of positive increments (grid, peer loop, paid gain); 40% for competitions
assumptions.basis: 2025 attribution is first-source only, not incremental [DS]. Peer, partner and paid channels touch the same students, and competitors come from partner and ambassador networks.
assumptions.sensitivity: Haircuts of 30% and 50%: base -102.

assumptions.value: 20% relative no-show reduction in base, 30% in stretch, applied to the 85% outside the holdout
assumptions.basis: RR 0.75 [SHOW-09]; 3-day plus 1-day reminders [SHOW-10]; ownership wording [SHOW-13]; plan-making +4.1 pp [SHOW-14]; bottom-up estimate of about 18% from the 117 leaked registrants plus reminders.
assumptions.sensitivity: Each 5 points of the reduction moves base by about 36 visitors.

assumptions.value: 15% of registration groups, randomised at squad level
assumptions.basis: One-sided test, alpha 0.05, 80% power: minimum detectable effect 5.2 pp at about 510 vs 2,890 [GRO-04 method]
assumptions.sensitivity: Costs 25 visitors in base. A 10% holdout would cost about 17 but raise the MDE to 6.2 pp.

assumptions.assumption: Paid and creator structural efficiency gain
assumptions.value: x1.20 base, x1.50 stretch registrations per rupee
assumptions.basis: Reels CPM about one-third of Feed [PAID-01]; free CTWA window [WA-03]; February is the low-CPM month [PAID-03]; regional micro creators get 2-3x engagement [INF-04]

drafts.big_idea: In Hyderabad, students turn up in batches, not from ads. So we recruit the batches: club charters in 32-44 partner colleges across the JNTUH/OU engineering belts, ambassadors and squads in the long tail, and a sponsor-funded competition league. Then we make it easy to actually arrive (WhatsApp reminders, a travel plan, college buses, the last metro). We do not buy reach.
drafts.north_star: Unique verified external visitors: distinct external people, deduplicated by phone/ID across both days, whose QR check-in was both admitted AND verified. This is the same rule used to count 2025's 2,050 [dataset]. Registrations are an input, not the goal [GRO-01]. Input-metric tree: (1) active chartered clubs x registrations per active club; (2) squad k-factor (net-new referred registrations per registrant); (3) T-7 reconfirm rate; (4) show rate by source and distance band; (5) cost per verified visitor. Every input is tracked weekly in the Growth Center dashboard.
city_rationale: Tier-1 by definition: Hyderabad (UA) is an X-class city under the 7th CPC HRA order [market:HYD-24].

Dense student supply: Hyderabad district has 465 colleges (4th in India) and Ranga Reddy 338 (9th) [market:HYD-04]. Telangana's GER is 46.6 vs India's 30.0 [market:HYD-02]. The metro has roughly 8 lakh students (ASSUMPTION: 1.6M+ Telangana students x ~50% in Hyderabad + Rangareddy [MED-19]). The base of 3,288 visitors is ~0.4% of that pool, so the market is not the constraint; conversion is.

Supply is clustered, which suits a partnership model: 107 of 175 engineering colleges sit in Hyderabad, Medchal-Malkajgiri and Ranga Reddy [market:HYD-11]. 130 JNTUH private colleges take 87,804 students a year (~675 per college) [market:HYD-08], 72% of engineering seats are CSE/allied [market:HYD-09], and IEEE Hyderabad lists 132 student branches [MED-18].

Local youth media is Telugu-first and based in Hyderabad: ChaiBisket (903K IG / 1.3M YT) and Wirally (846K IG / 1.8M YT) [MED-10, MED-11]. India's Meta CPMs run ~90% below the global level and were cheapest in February [PAID-03].
Cheaper than the other Tier-1 metros (Mercer 2024 rank 202 vs Bengaluru 195, Delhi 164, Mumbai 136) [market:HYD-27], so in-kind and sponsor budgets go further.

A clean date exists: Sat-Sun 13-14 Mar 2027 falls after the JNTUH II-IV mid-terms (1-6 Feb) and first-year mid-terms (3-9 Mar) [venue:HYD-01, HYD-02], after GATE (Feb weekends) [venue:HYD-07] and Eid (~10 Mar) [venue:HYD-04], and before Holi (22 Mar) [venue:HYD-05] and the April exams. It is also clear of the Elan (Jan) and Felicity/Pearl/Shruthi (Feb) window [fest-landscape].

Constraints are known and designed for: peripheral colleges, a 69 km metro with an 11 pm last train [venue:HYD-11], HITEX 2.6 km from HITEC City station [venue:HYD-15], a 10 pm outdoor-sound cut-off [venue:HYD-27], and Cyberabad CPPMS permissions (14 days ticketed / 10 days non-ticketed >500) [venue:HYD-26].

fest_dates_and_timeline.focus: Lock Sat-Sun 13-14 Mar 2027 at HITEX (sponsor-funded; fallbacks 20-21 Mar, 27-28 Feb). Stand up registration + QR + WhatsApp BSP and the Growth Center dashboard/copilot. Rank 107 metro-belt engineering colleges + large OU degree colleges by cluster, CSE intake and metro access. Sign 10 pilot charters in the two clusters nearest the venue (Kukatpally-Bachupally-Miyapur; Gandipet-Narsingi-Gachibowli). Open ambassador recruitment (60). Get Telugu-media/creator quotes and run authenticity screens. Start competition prize-pool sponsor pitches.

Scale charters to 38 signed (stretch ~55), cluster by cluster: Ghatkesar-Uppal (Blue Line east), LB Nagar-Ibrahimpatnam-Nadergul (Red Line SE), Maisammaguda-Dundigal-Kompally (north, bus-dependent), OU-Tarnaka-Secunderabad degree belt. Club leads collect batch interest (identified leads). Competition listings open 4 Jan. Light touch over Sankranti (~13-17 Jan). Prize-pool go/no-go 15 Jan. Line-up reveal after Elan's January window. File Cyberabad CPPMS permission by 29 Jan for 5,000 peak concurrent (43 days ahead vs the 10-14 day minimum). Send the HMRL late-train request.
No campus pushes during the JNTUH II-IV mid-terms (1-6 Feb). Ship club kits, shoot creator content at the pilot colleges, configure the A/B cells.

Registration + 'reserved for you' QR passes open 8 Feb (33 days out). The 2025 lead-time data favours this: confirmed registrants 0-30 days out showed 80.5-81.6% vs 72.1% for 31-60 days [dataset]. Weekday club mini-events (GATE takes the 13-14 and 20-21 Feb weekends). Media bursts in the cheap-CPM February window. Squad leaderboard live. 15 Feb MASTER CHECKPOINT: scale/change/stop per idea and release of the Rs 30k reserve. Competition registration closes 1 Mar. First-year pushes pause 3-9 Mar (their mid-terms). No iftar-hour activations during Ramadan (~9 Feb-10 Mar).

T-7 'keep or release your spot' reconfirmation and waitlist batch release (6 Mar). T-3 reminder on 9 Mar (moved off Eid on 10 Mar). T-1 travel plan with last-train time (12 Mar). College-bus manifests. Final capacity forecast = confirmed x segment show rate.

QR-verified entry (5 scan lanes + 1 manual lane) and a live dashboard. Pro-nite ends 9:45 pm; shuttle loop to HITEC City/Raidurg runs to 10:45 pm, before the 11 pm last train. Walk-in gate registration closes if the live count passes 4,500.

Reconcile unique verified visitors by source, cluster, college, club and test arm. Pay ambassador and squad tiers on verified check-ins only. Read out the holdout and A/B results. Run the retro and hand priors to the next edition.

Partner and peer channels deliver at ~Rs 46-59 per verified visitor (2025: Rs 69-108), i.e. stage slots, certificates, college buses and verified-tier merch replace cash. At 2025 unit costs the same Rs 3.3L would buy only ~3,360 visitors.

The extra Rs 30,000 over the Rs 3L budget is released at the 15 Feb checkpoint only if projected blended cost is <= Rs 80 per verified visitor. Marginal cost of the stretch over the base: Rs 30,000 / 1,661 extra visitors = Rs 18.

drafts.capacity: VENUE (ASSUMPTION; sponsor-funded, outside marketing cash): HITEX. Hall-4 seats 8,000 theatre-style (main stage / pro-nite), Halls 1-3 seat 2,500 each (competitions, club showcases), Lawn 2,800 [venue:HYD-16]. The Lawn is too small for a stretch pro-nite, so the pro-nite goes in Hall-4. PEAK CONCURRENCY: in 2025, day 1 held 69.8% of all unique visitors (1,430/2,050) and the peak entry hour carried 17.6% of day-1 entrants (251/1,430) [dataset]. Dwell time is not in the data, so ASSUME 70% of day-1 externals are present at the evening peak, plus ~800 organising-college students and ~300 crew/artists. Base: day-1 externals 3,288 x 0.698 = 2,294 -> peak 2,294 x 0.70 + 1,100 = 2,706. Stretch: 4,949 x 0.698 = 3,452 -> 3,517. Even at 90% presence the stretch peak is 4,207. PERMISSION: file on Cyberabad CPPMS by 29 Jan 2027 for 5,000 peak concurrent (1.4x the stretch peak). Entry is free, but we file under the 14-day ticketed rule [venue:HYD-26] so the Rs 99 refundable priority-pass test cannot change the approver. HARD CAPS, because unmanaged demand has gone wrong before: Malla Reddy had permission for 7,000 and drew ~20,000 [fest:HYD-13]; Mood Indigo cancelled pre-registrations and shut out outsiders [NAT-01]. Entry is QR-only. Registrations close at 8,000 (8,000 x 81.5% x 0.698 x 0.70 + 1,100 = ~4,290 peak, under 5,000). Gate walk-in registration closes when the live count passes 4,500. THROUGHPUT: the stretch peak entry hour is ~606 externals (17.6% x 3,452). That needs 5 QR lanes at ~150 scans/hour (ASSUMPTION) plus 1 manual lane (2025 had 9.4% manual admissions [dataset]). TRANSPORT: the metro carries ~4.5 lakh/day [market:HYD-28], so ~3,500 extra riders is under 1% and not binding. The binding last mile is HITEX being 2.6 km from HITEC City station, the 10 pm outdoor-sound cut-off and the 11 pm last train. So the pro-nite ends 9:45 pm and the shuttle loop runs to 10:45 pm, and we ask HMRL for a late train (precedents: 1 am NYE, 12:30 am IPL [venue:HYD-12]). CONCLUSION: the stretch fits with ~25-40% headroom. The binding constraint is partner supply and the police permission number, not floor space.

framework.name: ICE (Impact, Confidence, Ease; Sean Ellis) [GRO-03]: average of three 1-10 scores, ties broken on cost per incremental verified visitor
framework.how_scored: IMPACT = base incremental verified visitors / 75, rounded, capped at 10: I1 730 -> 10; I5 298 -> 4; I2 277 -> 4; I4 250 -> 3; I3 198 -> 3. CONFIDENCE = evidence grade: 8 = RCT/field evidence plus measured 2025 leak, effect size discounted; 7 = channel economics measured in the 2025 dataset plus one untested assumption; 5 = external benchmarks only; 4 = no rate cards or prior data and the weakest 2025 show rate. EASE = 10 minus cash share, team-hours and hard external dependencies (MoUs, sponsor money, template approvals). SCORES (I, C, E -> average): I1 Club Charter 10, 7, 4 -> 7.0; I3 Show-up engine 3, 8, 9 -> 6.7; I2 Squad/Ambassadors 4, 7, 7 -> 6.0; I5 Competition League 4, 5, 5 -> 4.7; I4 Telugu media/CTWA 3, 4, 7 -> 4.7. Tie broken on cost per incremental visitor: I5 Rs 84 vs I4 Rs 240, so I5 ranks 4th. DECISIONS: double down on I1 (largest, best-measured channel) and I3 (cheapest, highest-confidence lever, protects every other idea). Invest in I2 as the loop that compounds I1. Run I5 behind a sponsor gate. Cap I4 at 20% of cash with a stop-loss. Re-score every idea at the 15 Feb checkpoint with Hyderabad actuals replacing 2025 priors.

ideas.name: Club Charter Network (double down)
ideas.concept: Turn 'college partnerships' from a poster-and-MoU channel into club-level charters, signed cluster by cluster along the metro corridors. Order: Kukatpally-Bachupally-Miyapur (Red Line) and Gandipet-Narsingi-Gachibowli (nearest HITEX) first, then Ghatkesar-Uppal (Blue Line east), LB Nagar-Ibrahimpatnam-Nadergul (Red Line SE), Maisammaguda-Dundigal-Kompally (north) and the OU-Tarnaka-Secunderabad degree belt. In each of 38 colleges (32 active), 2-3 clubs (IEEE branch, E-cell, NSS unit, dance/music club) sign a charter. They get a hosted slot (showcase stall, a competition track they co-run, stage time), certificates and a public 'Club Cup' for the most VERIFIED attendees. In return they run an internal push (class announcements, club WhatsApp groups, one weekday mini-event) with a batch code and a target of 20 registrations. Far-cluster colleges lend a Saturday bus in kind; we reimburse fuel.
ideas.why_it_works: It was the best measured channel in 2025: 90.0% identified-to-registered, 85.6% registered-to-visited, 91.7% confirmed-to-visited, 4.5% CTR, Rs 81 per visitor [dataset]. Its volume was limited by operations, not demand: 64, 77, 80, 97 registrations a week in weeks 11-14 vs 21, 8, 0 in weeks 8-10 when its spend postings stopped (4-28 Feb) [dataset]. Hyderabad supply is dense and clustered: 107 metro-belt engineering colleges [market:HYD-11], ~675 freshers per JNTUH college per year [market:HYD-08], 132 IEEE branches [MED-18]. Clubs formalise the group decision 70% of Gen Z already make [MED-25], and paying in stage time and recognition rather than cash keeps the cost down.
ideas.contribution_math: Base: 32 active colleges x 2.5 clubs x 20 registrations = 1,600 x 80% show = 1,280 verified, minus the 550 that 2025 partnerships (385) + community groups (165) delivered (already in the 1,535 floor) = +730. Stretch: 44 x 3 x 20 = 2,640 x 80% = 2,112 - 550 = +1,562. The 80% show rate is a haircut from the 2025 partner+community blend of 84.6%, because newer colleges and clubs will be weaker. Sensitivity: +/-5 registrations per club = +/-400 base visitors.

Randomise the incentive at college level, 5 vs 5: stage slot only vs stage slot + public Club Cup leaderboard. Read registrations per club at day 10 and verified show by batch code after the event. Expand to the far clusters only if the pilot median is >= 12 registrations per club by day 10.

ideas.stop_threshold: < 8 registrations per club at 15 Feb after one change cycle, OR a cluster projecting > Rs 150 per verified visitor -> stop new charters in that cluster and move its captain to ambassador coverage (I2).

ideas.name: Last-mile Show-up Engine (double down)
ideas.concept: One WhatsApp-first system for every registrant: an instant 'reserved for you' QR pass; a plan-making step (which day, which metro station or college bus, with whom); a T-7 'keep or release your spot' reconfirmation that refills spots from the waitlist in batches; reminders at T-3, T-1 (travel plan + 11 pm last-train time) and the morning of the event. Programming is set around the metro: pro-nite ends 9:45 pm and shuttles run to HITEC City/Raidurg until 10:45 pm. Test cell: a Rs 99 refundable pro-nite priority pass, returned as food credit at check-in.
ideas.why_it_works: 2025 lost 31% of registrants. 117 (4.2%) were waitlisted or never confirmed and attended at 0%; the one generic nurture email showed no lift (69.0% vs 68.7%) and a 12.7% opt-out [dataset]. Reminder evidence is strong: text reminders cut no-shows by 25% (RR 0.75) [SHOW-09], two reminders beat one [SHOW-10], 'reserved for you' ownership wording performed best [SHOW-13], and plan-making added +4.1pp [SHOW-14]. Utility messages cost ~Rs 0.115 [WA-01]. Hyderabad's last mile is real: HITEX is 2.6 km from metro, the last train leaves at 11 pm and outdoor sound stops at 10 pm.
ideas.contribution_math: The lift is applied ONCE, to total registrations, after source show rates (which are 2025 rates with no reminders). Base +5pp x 3,950 = 198; stretch +6pp x 5,919 = 355. The +5pp is built from: reminders +3pp (RR 0.75 on a ~25% no-show is ~6pp, halved for transfer from health trials); leak recovery +1.5pp (half of the 4.2% 2025 waitlist/unconfirmed leak, shown at ~77%); plan-making +0.5pp (vs 4.1pp in the voting trial). The stretch adds +0.5pp each from reminders and plan-making. Ceiling: blended registered-to-visited of 80.1% base / 81.5% stretch, under the 82% large-paid-event median [SHOW-02]. Rs 101 per incremental visitor, below the marginal acquisition channel (media, Rs 240).
ideas.resources: Owner 3 (Show-up & Ops lead, also owns permissions and check-in); 1 volunteer on the WhatsApp inbox; the growth APM runs the randomisation and the forecast.
ideas.timeline: Dec: BSP onboarding, template approval, plan-making form. 8 Feb: passes and plan-making go live with registration. 6 Mar: T-7 reconfirm and waitlist batch release. 9 Mar: T-3 (moved off Eid on 10 Mar). 12 Mar: T-1. 13-14 Mar: morning-of. 15-20 Mar: experiment read-out.
ideas.test_design: 2x2 factorial at registrant level: ownership/loss wording vs neutral, x plan-making prompt vs none. Each main effect uses all ~3,950 registrants split 50/50, giving a minimum detectable effect of ~3.9pp (80% power, alpha 0.05, baseline 75%). Plus a 10% no-T-3 holdout as a directional check (MDE ~6.4pp; sample-size logic per [GRO-04]). Deposit cell: Rs 99 refundable vs free priority pass, randomised among pro-nite pass requesters; read take-up and show rate.
kpis: T-7 reconfirm rate (target >=85%)
Plan completion: day + station/bus + companions (target >=60%)
WhatsApp read rate (>=85%) and opt-out (<3%)
Waitlist spots released and filled
Show rate by test arm and by distance band
2025-proven leading indicators: programme download (74.7% vs 61.9% show) and question submitted (79.4% vs 68.0%)
ideas.framework_scores: ICE: I=3 (+198 base), C=8 (RCT evidence + measured 2025 leak; effect halved), E=9 (Rs 20k, off-the-shelf tools, no partner dependency) -> 6.7, rank 2
ideas.dependencies_risks_overlap: DEPENDS ON WhatsApp opt-in captured at registration, template approval lead time, and clean phone numbers. The T-3 send moves off Eid (10 Mar). RISKS: message fatigue and opt-outs; a template classed as marketing (Rs 0.86) instead of utility (Rs 0.115) raises cost ~7x; if the deposit cell is read as ticketing it changes the police approver, which is why we file under the 14-day rule. OVERLAP: none with the source ideas, because the lift is counted once on total registrations. Squad social pressure (I2) and plan-making both work on solo deciders, so that interaction is read in the factorial.
ideas.critical_variables: T-7 reconfirm rate, plan completion rate, opt-out rate, share of registrants in far distance bands.
ideas.early_success_signal: By 20 Feb: >= 60% plan completion and >= 85% read rate. By T-7: ownership arm reconfirm >= 3pp above neutral.
ideas.early_failure_signal: Opt-out > 5% after the first reminder; T-7 reconfirm < 70%; far-cluster registrants reconfirming > 10pp below near clusters.
ideas.scale_threshold: Reconfirm >= 85% -> overbook the pro-nite zone to capacity / forecast show rate and release the waitlist earlier. Deposit cell show >= 8pp above free with take-up >= 40% -> extend it to the whole priority tier.
ideas.change_threshold: Reconfirm 70-85% -> add a squad-leader nudge and a travel-cost message. Far-cluster gap > 10pp -> add a college bus or a metro-fare credit for that cluster.
ideas.stop_threshold: Opt-out > 8% -> cut to 2 touches (T-1 + morning-of; two reminders still beat one [SHOW-10]). Deposit cell reduces pass take-up > 30% with no show gain -> drop it.
ideas.action_on_change: Daily in the final week: forecast = confirmed x arm/segment show rate. Forecast above capacity -> release fewer waitlist spots. Forecast below -> release more and push squad nudges.
ideas.dashboard_ai_support: Dashboard: reconfirm curve by day, live forecast vs capacity and permission, arm comparison with confidence intervals, show rate by distance band. Copilot: answers 'if T-7 reconfirm ends at 78%, how many waitlist spots do we release?' (capacity / forecast show rate), proposes the release as a task for approval, and says when a sample is too small to call a winner.

ideas.name: Squad Pass + verified-check-in ambassador leaderboard
ideas.concept: Make the squad the unit of registration. Every confirmed registrant gets a Squad Pass link; a squad of 4+ who ALL check in unlocks fast-lane entry and a priority pro-nite zone (in-kind), and the squad leader gets merch. In the ~70 metro-belt colleges and larger degree colleges without a charter, recruit 60 campus ambassadors (1 per college) on IIT Ropar-style tiers (certificate -> social mention -> T-shirt -> free perks) [CA-01]. Every reward is paid on verified check-ins, never on raw sign-ups.
ideas.why_it_works: 2025 referrals were the cheapest channel (Rs 69 per visitor, 78.6% show) and ambassadors delivered 19% of visitors at Rs 108 [dataset]. Squads add a social cost to not turning up: seeing that others can see you vote raised turnout +8.1pp [SHOW-15], and 59% of Gen Z skip events where they know no one [SHOW-16]. Paying on check-ins removes the incentive to pad sign-ups. Ambassadors cover the long tail the charter team cannot reach.
ideas.contribution_math: Ambassadors: 42 active of 60 (70%) x 15 registrations = 630 x 75% (2025 show) = 472. Squads: k = 0.35 share x 3 friends x 0.17 conversion = 0.1785 (2025 implied 350/2,450 = 0.143) x 3,352 non-referral registrations = 598 net new x 78.6% = 470. Gross 942 - 665 (2025 ambassadors 390 + referrals 275, in the floor) = +277. Stretch: 56 x 15 = 840 x 75% = 630; k = 0.40 x 3 x 0.17 = 0.204 x 4,916 = 1,003 x 78.6% = 788; 1,418 - 665 = +753. Overlap removed: 25% of squad-link registrations already held another code (base 199 registrations / 156 visitors; stretch 334 / 262).
ideas.resources: Owner 2 (Community lead); 2 volunteers for ambassador support; an ambassador WhatsApp Community; referral links built into the registration form.
ideas.timeline: Recruit ambassadors 1-20 Dec; onboard by 10 Jan; leaderboard live when registration opens on 8 Feb; tier payouts after check-in reconciliation (15-20 Mar).
ideas.test_design: Randomise at registrant level, 50/50: (A) squad unlock (fast lane + priority zone at 4 verified) vs (B) individual referral merch; read the k-factor and the squad vs solo show rate. Ambassadors: reward-on-verified vs reward-on-registration in 2 matched clusters for 2 weeks, then roll out the winner.

Squad share of registrations (target >=40%)
Squad vs solo show rate
Ambassadors active (>=5 registrations in 14 days; target 70%)
Duplicate/fake rate (same phone, college mismatch) <=5%
Cost per verified visitor (target <=Rs 60)

ideas.dependencies_risks_overlap: DEPENDS ON the registrant base from I1/I4/I5 (k x base), so it compounds them and shrinks when they miss. RISKS: fake sign-ups to climb the leaderboard; ambassadors drifting after ~3 weeks. OVERLAP: ambassadors are barred from charter colleges; squad credit goes only to net-new phones; competition supporter passes are counted here, not in I5.

ideas.early_success_signal: k >= 0.15 within 10 days of registration opening; >= 30 ambassadors active by 20 Feb; squad reconfirm >= 5pp above solo.
ideas.early_failure_signal: k < 0.08 by 18 Feb; < 50% of ambassadors active at day 14; duplicate rate > 5%.
ideas.scale_threshold: k >= 0.20 AND ambassador cost <= Rs 60 per verified visitor at 15 Feb -> recruit 20 more ambassadors (stretch) and add a front-zone squad perk.
ideas.change_threshold: k 0.08-0.15 -> switch all registrants to the winning reward arm and add a 'bring 3 friends' nudge at T-7.
ideas.stop_threshold: k < 0.08 after the change, or duplicate rate > 10% -> stop merch rewards and keep only certificate tiers on verified check-ins.
ideas.action_on_change: Weekly: deactivate dormant ambassadors and reassign their colleges; if fraud rises, tighten verification (OTP + college ID at the gate); redirect unspent reward budget to I1 buses.
ideas.dashboard_ai_support: Dashboard: k-factor trend, squad-size histogram, ambassador leaderboard (confirmed before the event, verified after), fraud flags. Copilot: answers 'which ambassadors went quiet this week?' and proposes reassignment tasks for approval; recomputes projected visitors if k drops to 0.10.

ideas.name: Inter-college Competition League (sponsor-gated)
ideas.concept: A sponsor-funded league with online prelims on Unstop and on-site rounds at the fest, built for a CSE-heavy city: a 24-hour AI hackathon (50 teams x 4), BGMI/Valorant esports (48 squads x 4) and Battle of Bands / dance-crew rounds (30 crews x 6). Every member registers by name, and every registered team plays an on-site round, so registering commits them to turning up. GCC sponsors fund prizes and give finalists interview fast-tracks. IIT-H, IIIT-H and BITS-H provide judges and mentors for credibility.
ideas.why_it_works: 72% of engineering seats are CSE/allied [market:HYD-09] and Hyderabad has ~515 GCCs [market:HYD-26]. Hyderabad fests pull participants with prize pools (Elan Rs 16L [fest:HYD-02], Infinium Rs 12.2L [fest:HYD-06], Sintillashunz Rs 5L+ [fest:HYD-12]), and Comic Con drew gamers with BGMI lobbies [fest:HYD-17]. Teams have a stake, the same commitment that cuts no-shows at paid events (17% vs 28%) [SHOW-01].

Stretch: (70x4 + 64x4 + 40x6) = 776 x 0.65 = 504 x 80% = 403. Overlap removed: 200 registrations / 160 visitors base; 272 / 218 stretch. Rs 84 per incremental visitor.
ideas.resources: Owner 5 (Competitions & Sponsors lead); 6 volunteer event heads; tracks co-run with chartered IEEE branches and E-cells (shared with I1); Halls 1-3 for on-site rounds.
ideas.timeline: Dec: pitch prize pool and GCC fast-track to sponsors. 4 Jan: listings open. 15 Jan: prize-pool go/no-go. 8-28 Feb: online prelims on weekdays (GATE is on the 13-14 and 20-21 Feb weekends). 1 Mar: registration closes. 13-14 Mar: on-site rounds and finals.
ideas.test_design: Go/no-go gate: prize pool >= Rs 1.5L confirmed by 15 Jan, else shrink to 2 competitions with trophies + GCC interview fast-track. A/B in half the competitions: 'team + 2 supporter passes' bundle vs team-only; supporters are attributed to I2 to avoid double counting.

Copilot: answers 'which competitions are behind target, and is the gap in charter or non-charter colleges?' and drafts a circular task for the right owner, written after approval.

ideas.name: Telugu youth media + cluster nano-creators via Click-to-WhatsApp (test small, scale only on threshold)
ideas.concept: Replace broad paid social and creator partners with: one Telugu youth-media collab (ChaiBisket or Wirally, part barter: passes, a stage segment, content rights); 4 Hyderabad nano/micro creators drawn from partner-college clusters (>= 3% engagement, audience-authenticity screened); and Reels Click-to-WhatsApp ads geo-fenced to the engineering belts. All of it lands in the WhatsApp registration flow. Creative is bilingual Telugu-English and meme-native, with female-led creators to offset Instagram's ~70% male ad audience [MED-01].
ideas.why_it_works: City-wide awareness needs some reach beyond the partner network, but the 2025 versions were the worst channels. Paid social cost Rs 274 per visitor, showed at 50%, had 12.2% opt-out and burned out after week 9 (105-124 registrations a week, then 35 at the same Rs 14,400 spend); creators cost Rs 337 [dataset]. Reels CPM is Rs 45-140 vs Feed Rs 150-350 [PAID-01]. CTWA opens a free 7-day messaging window [WA-03]. Regional micro-creators get 2-3x the engagement at ~1/10 the cost [INF-04]. ChaiBisket and Wirally are Hyderabad-based [MED-10, MED-11].
ideas.contribution_math: New line (paid social and creators were removed from the floor). Base: Rs 60,000 / Rs 120 per registration = 500 x 50% show = 250. Stretch: Rs 75,000 / Rs 110 = 682 x 50% = 341. Rs 120 is 19% better than 2025's blended Rs 148 per registration (paid Rs 137, creators Rs 169) because of the Reels/CTWA mix. Show is held at 2025's 50% because there is no evidence it improves. Only WhatsApp-keyword/UTM first touches count; assisted conversions get no credit. Rs 240 per verified visitor vs Rs 295 for 2025 paid+creators.
ideas.resources: Owner 4 (Content & Media lead); 2 volunteer editors; content is shot at I1 club mini-events, so it also serves the charters.
ideas.timeline: Dec: quotes and authenticity screens. Jan: shoot at pilot charter colleges. Two bursts, 8-21 Feb and 22 Feb-5 Mar, in the seasonally cheap February CPM window [PAID-03]. Creative rotates weekly to avoid a repeat of the 2025 week-9 burnout.
ideas.test_design: Geo holdout: run CTWA in 3 clusters and keep 2 dark for the first 14 days; compare registrations from non-partner colleges (difference-in-differences). Each creator gets a unique WhatsApp keyword; after week 1, cut the bottom half by cost per registration. Telugu vs English creative split 50/50.

CTWA chat starts and cost per chat
Weekly CTR trend (fatigue alert at -30% week over week)
T-7 reconfirm rate of media registrants (>=75%)
Verified show rate (>=50%)
Female share of media registrants
ideas.framework_scores: ICE: I=3 (+250 base), C=4 (no Telugu-media rate cards found; this channel showed 50% in 2025), E=7 (fast to launch and stop) -> 4.7. Tied with I5; ranked 5th on cost per incremental visitor (Rs 240 vs Rs 84)
ideas.dependencies_risks_overlap: DEPENDS ON quotes and barter acceptance (no public rate cards). ~1 in 4 creator profiles fail authenticity screens [INF-04]. RISKS: low show rate, creative fatigue, male skew. OVERLAP: its awareness also helps I1/I2 conversions but is deliberately not credited; first-touch keyword only. That understates this idea, which is the conservative direction.

ideas.early_success_signal: Burst 1 at <= Rs 120 per registration; lit clusters >= 15% above dark clusters; media registrants reconfirm >= 75% at T-7.
ideas.early_failure_signal: > Rs 180 per registration for 7 days, CTR down > 30% week over week, or dark clusters registering as well as lit ones (no incrementality).
ideas.scale_threshold: <= Rs 100 per registration AND reconfirm >= 75% -> move the stretch top-up (+Rs 15k) into CTWA.
ideas.change_threshold: Rs 120-180 per registration -> rotate creative, shift spend to the best creator keyword, change the Telugu/English mix.
ideas.stop_threshold: > Rs 180 per registration after one rotation, or no geo lift -> stop paid, keep only barter content, and move the cash to I1 buses or I2 rewards.
ideas.action_on_change: Weekly creative rotation; budget moves between creators by keyword; the 15 Feb checkpoint decides whether this line grows or is cut.
ideas.dashboard_ai_support: Dashboard: spend vs registrations by creator/keyword, CTR decay chart, geo-holdout comparison, projected cost per verified visitor using the source show rate. Copilot: flags fatigue ('CTR fell 35% week over week, the same pattern as 2025 week 10') and drafts a rotation task for approval; refuses to sum daily reported reach into unique reach (a known dataset limitation).

drafts.overlap_adjustment: RULE 1, one person = one source: registrants are de-duplicated by phone number and keep the source of their first registration. If a competition participant already registered with a club batch code, they stay with I1. Squad links credit I2 only for phone numbers not already registered or coded. Creator keywords and CTWA credit I4 only on first touch, with no assisted credit. RULE 2, replacement accounting: I1 and I2 replace 2025 channels that are already in the 1,535 floor (2,050 minus the 515 visitors from dropped paid social and creators). So only their net delta counts: I1 1,280 - 550 = +730; I2 942 - 665 = +277. I4 and I5 are new lines and count in full. RULE 3, the show-up lift is counted once: I3's +5pp (stretch +6pp) is applied once to total registrations, after source show rates taken from 2025 when there were no reminders. It is not baked into any source's show rate. RULE 4, explicit deductions: I5 drops 35% of participants as already club-coded (base 200 registrations / 160 visitors; stretch 272 / 218). I2 drops 25% of squad-link registrations as already coded (base 199 / 156; stretch 334 / 262). Total removed: 316 visitors base, 480 stretch. RULE 5, ceiling: blended registered-to-visited is held at or under PheedLoop's 82% large-paid-event median (80.1% base, 81.5% stretch). SUMS: base 1,535 + 730 + 277 + 198 + 250 + 298 = 3,288; stretch 1,535 + 1,562 + 753 + 355 + 341 + 403 = 4,949. DEPENDENCY NOTE: I2's squad referrals scale with the registrant base from I1/I4/I5 (k x base), so if I1 misses, I2 misses with it. The downside run (I1 at 15 registrations per club, k at 0.143, lift +2pp, media at Rs 148) gives 2,638.

deprioritized.idea: Broad interest-targeted paid social (Feed ads)
deprioritized.reason: 2025: Rs 274 per verified visitor, 50% show, 12.2% opt-out, and it burned out after week 9 (105-124 registrations a week, then 35 at the same Rs 14,400 spend) [dataset]. Paid social + creators took 55.4% of spend for 25.1% of visitors. Cut from Rs 93k to Rs 15k of geo-fenced CTWA inside I4.

deprioritized.idea: Macro influencers / celebrity creator posts
deprioritized.reason: Rs 2-12 lakh per Reel [INF-01], so one post would consume the whole budget. 2025 creator partners were the worst channel at Rs 337 per visitor [dataset]. Replaced by 4 nano/micro creators + 1 Telugu media barter.

deprioritized.idea: Generic nurture email blasts
deprioritized.reason: No measurable lift in 2025 (69.0% vs 68.7% show) and a 12.7% opt-out [dataset]. Indian M&E broadcast email gets 2.19% click-to-open [EMAIL-01]. Email is kept only for triggered messages.

deprioritized.idea: Paid stalls or sponsorship at other colleges' fests
deprioritized.reason: Rs 15k-2L per placement [PART-01] with no verified-attendance path. Club charters (I1) co-host in kind instead.

deprioritized.idea: Charging for general entry to raise show rate
deprioritized.reason: Hyderabad's big fests are free to enter [fest:HYD-03], so a fee cuts reach. Within the same event, payers show only 2-4pp more [SHOW-04]. Kept only as a Rs 99 refundable priority-pass test cell in I3.

deprioritized.idea: Headliner-led growth (bigger star as the acquisition lever)
deprioritized.reason: Venue and production are sponsor-funded and out of scope. Hyderabad fests recycle the same acts within weeks [fest:HYD-09]. Ungated star demand caused the Malla Reddy overcrowding (7k permitted, ~20k came) [fest:HYD-13]. A fresh act is booked for novelty, but no visitors are credited to it.

deprioritized.idea: Young professionals / GCC evening segment
deprioritized.reason: Would dilute the student-first North Star and needs a separate ticketed product. GCCs are used as competition sponsors (I5) instead.

deprioritized.idea: Intermediate (Class 11-12) students
deprioritized.reason: Theory exams run 24 Feb-20 Mar 2027 [venue:HYD-08].

deprioritized.idea: Flagship residential campuses as a volume source
deprioritized.reason: ~19,000 students in total, far from HITEX, with their own Jan-Feb fests. Used as judges, mentors and content partners only.

deprioritized.idea: Mall flashmobs / Numaish activations
deprioritized.reason: Reach with no verifiable registration path. Numaish ends mid-February; Felicity's Lulu flashmob drew 750 onlookers [fest:HYD-05], not registrants. Used only as content for I4.

assumptions.sensitivity: +/-5 per club = +/-400 base visitors (2,888 to 3,687). Largest single swing; tested by the 10-college pilot at day 10.
