headline_numbers: BASE: 3,288 unique verified external visitors (+60% vs 2,050 in 2025) on Rs 3,00,000 -> Rs 91 per verified visitor (2025: Rs 134, -32%).

STRETCH: 4,949 (+141%) on Rs 3,30,000 -> Rs 67 per visitor. The extra comes from supply (44 active colleges x 3 clubs, squad k 0.20, +6pp show), not money: at 2025 unit costs Rs 3.3L buys only ~3,360.
Triangulated: bottom-up base 3,288 vs 3,245 (2025 mix with paid/creator money moved to partner channels) vs 3,028 (2025 unit costs, no efficiency gain). Downside run: 2,638, still +29% on 2025.
Registrations 3,950 base / 5,919 stretch. Registered-to-visited goes from 68.8% (2025) to 80.1% base / 81.5% stretch, held under the 82% large-paid-event median.
68% of base visitors come from partner supply: club batches 1,280 + ambassadors 472 + squads 470 = 2,222 of 3,288.
Cut: paid social + creators took 55.4% of 2025 spend for 25.1% of visitors; the 2027 media line is Rs 60k (20%) with a stop-loss at Rs 180 per registration.
Overlap removed: 316 double-claimed visitors in the base, 480 in the stretch. The five ideas sum exactly onto the 1,535 floor.
Capacity: stretch peak ~3,520 concurrent vs HITEX Hall-4's 8,000; police permission for 5,000 filed by 29 Jan; QR hard cap at 8,000 registrations; 5+1 entry lanes.
Decision gate: 15 Feb 2027 checkpoint, about 4 weeks out. Every idea has scale/change/stop thresholds, and the Rs 30k reserve goes only to winners.

drafts.big_idea: Buy attendance, not registrations. In 2025, 875 people registered and never came (2,800 registered, 1,925 attended). First we close that gap with a WhatsApp commitment engine costing Rs 20k. Then we move Rs 97k out of paid social and creators, whose registrants showed up only 50% of the time, into Hyderabad's campus clusters and friend squads, whose registrants showed up 79-86% of the time.
drafts.north_star: Unique verified external visitors: QR check-ins that are both admitted and verified, deduplicated across the two days. 2025: 2,050. 2027: base 2,832, stretch 3,530. Input-metric tree: (1) share of registrations from high-show sources (partners, clubs, ambassadors, squads): at least 75%, base 80%, 2025 54%; (2) share of registrants holding a live pass at T-0: 89.3% to 93.8%; (3) confirmed-to-check-in rate, forecast weekly from T-7 reconfirmations: 77.0% to 86.3%; (4) rupees per verified visitor: Rs 134 to Rs 106 or less. Guardrails: forecast peak on site no more than 90% of the police-permitted number, and WhatsApp opt-out no more than 3%. Registrations are an input, never the goal [GRO-01].
city_rationale: Hyderabad is officially Tier-1: Hyderabad (UA) is an X-class city under the 7th CPC HRA order [MKT HYD-24].

It is the densest student market after Bengaluru. Hyderabad district has 465 colleges (4th in India) and Ranga Reddy has 338 (9th) [MKT HYD-04]. Telangana has 17.87 lakh higher-education students [MKT HYD-01] and a GER of 46.6 against 30.0 for India [MKT HYD-02].

Students are concentrated and lean to tech, which suits a cluster model. 107 of Telangana's 175 engineering colleges are in Hyderabad, Medchal-Malkajgiri and Ranga Reddy [MKT HYD-11]. 83,622 of 1,16,877 engineering seats are CSE or allied [MKT HYD-09], so AI/GCC workshops are the natural hook and about 515 GCCs [MKT HYD-26] are natural sponsors.

It is the cheapest Tier-1 city to run in: Mercer 2024 ranks Hyderabad 202, against Bengaluru 195, Delhi 164 and Mumbai 136 [MKT HYD-27]. India's Meta CPMs were at their lowest in February [PAID-03], which is exactly our sprint window.

The conversion rails already exist. 99.5% of 15-29-year-olds who bank online can use UPI [MED-22]. WhatsApp utility messages cost about Rs 0.115 each [WA-01]. Telugu youth media brands (ChaiBisket, Wirally) are based in Hyderabad [MED-10/11]. There are 132 IEEE student branches for club-led distribution [MED-18].

We plan around the city's real constraints rather than reach. The metro covers only 69 km and the last train leaves at 11 pm [VEN HYD-11]. Outdoor sound must stop by 10 pm [VEN HYD-27]. HITEX is 2.6 km from HITEC City station [VEN HYD-15]. The fest season is crowded: Elan in January, Felicity and Pearl in February [FEST HYD-01/04/07]. Our target is under 0.6% of the roughly 5.9 lakh priority pool, so the binding limit is getting people to show up, not reach.

fest_dates_and_timeline.focus: This is the only weekend clear of all of these: JNTUH II-IV year mid-terms (1-6 Feb) [VEN HYD-01], first-year mid-terms (3-9 Mar) [VEN HYD-02], GATE (6-21 Feb) [VEN HYD-07], Shivaratri (6 Mar) and Eid (~10 Mar) [VEN HYD-04/05]. It also falls before Holi (22 Mar) and the April exams. If the IPL fixtures (possible start 10 Mar) [VEN HYD-09] put an SRH home match at Uppal on 13-14 Mar, move to 20-21 Mar. The pro-nite is indoors in HITEX Hall-4 and ends at 9:45 pm, ahead of the 10 pm sound rule and the 11 pm last metro.

Onboard the WhatsApp BSP and get Meta template approval. Set up Luma or KonfHub for registration and QR passes, the holdout randomiser and the dashboard. Geocode the 107 metro engineering colleges and the top degree colleges into 5 clusters, shortlist 60, pair them and randomise them into waves. Recruit 45 ambassadors and 5 cluster leads. The sponsor holds the venue (HITEX). Draft the CPPMS police application.

Sign 20 partner MOUs by Wed 6 Jan. Registration opens Mon 4 Jan. Run the squad-first vs solo-first A/B (4-24 Jan) and the commitment-ladder and deposit test (4 Jan - 8 Feb). Wave-1 pre-fest club workshops double as early test beds for the reminder engine. Pause pushes over Sankranti (13-17 Jan) [FEST HYD-21]. Gate 1 is Mon 18 Jan (registrations target 500, i.e. 15% of the final count).

Reach 40 MOUs by 31 Jan. File the Cyberabad CPPMS permission by Fri 22 Jan, seven weeks ahead of the 14-day legal minimum [VEN HYD-26]. 1-6 Feb is a quiet week (mid-terms): only the WhatsApp engine runs, with no campus activations. Gate 2 is Mon 8 Feb (target 1,337 registrations, 40%), where budget tranches and the contingency are decided.

This is peak acquisition. The median time from first contact to registration is 7 days, so acquisition must peak at least two weeks out. No weekend activations on the GATE weekends (13-14 and 20-21 Feb). Community activations run after iftar during Ramadan (from about 9 Feb). Gate 3 is Mon 22 Feb (target 2,173 registrations, 65%), where we set overbooking ratios and recheck the forecast against the permit. Bus go/no-go is Wed 3 Mar (T-10). Paid stops on 5 Mar.

Sat 6 Mar (T-7, target 3,076 registrations): reconfirm-or-release message and the first waitlist batch. Messages to first-years stay light during their 3-9 Mar mid-terms. The T-3 touch moves to Thu 11 Mar because Eid is about 10 Mar. T-1 goes on Fri 12 Mar, plus a morning-of message. The fest runs 13-14 Mar with QR-only gates, and the Day-2 waitlist batch is sized from the Day-1 gate count.
Read out the holdout and every A/B. Report cost per verified visitor by idea. Record what to scale or kill for 2028.

base_case.arithmetic: (1) Registrations from spend / CPR. Below each channel's 2025 spend the 2025 CPR applies; above it, CPR is 1.25x. Partners: 31,000/68.9 + 59,000/86.1 = 450 + 685 = 1,135. Ambassadors: 42,000/80.8 = 520. Clubs: 16,000/80 + 4,000/100 = 240. Organic: 14,000/56 = 250. CTWA: 40,000/120 = 333. Creators: 15,000/150 = 100. Seeds = 2,578. Squad multiplier k = 0.19 x 2.6 x 0.60 = 0.296, so 2,578 x 0.296 = 764 net-new. Total = 3,343. (2) Visitors from the mix alone, at 2025 channel show rates, with volume above 2025 levels showing 10 points lower: partners 385 + 685 x 0.756 = 903; ambassadors 520 x 0.75 = 390; clubs 165 + 40 x 0.725 = 194; organic 195; CTWA 333 x 0.50 = 167; creators 50; squads 275 + 414 x 0.686 = 559. Total 2,457 (73.5%). (3) Leakage: the 26.5% no-show x 34.3% (2025: 300 of 875 no-shows never reached a live pass) = 9.08%, so confirmed share is 90.9% and confirmed show-up is 80.9%. Idea 4 recovers 31.4% of the 304 leakers: 95 x 0.809 = +77, and confirmed becomes 3,135 (93.8%). (4) Engine: 3,135 x 19.1% x 20% x 85% = +102. Squads: 53% members x 10% of residual no-show = +26. Ladder: 3,135 x 15.0% x 0.40 x 0.25 x 0.80 = +38. Bus: 85 riders x 14.3% x 50% = +6. Registered visitors = 2,707 (81.0% of registered). Plus 125 walk-ins = 2,832. (5) Growth vs 2025 is +782. Of that, (3,343 - 2,800) x 68.75% = 373 comes from more registrations, and 3,343 x (81.0% - 68.75%) = 408 (52%) comes from better show-up among people who already registered.

drafts.capacity: Venue: HITEX, in the Cyberabad IT corridor. Production is sponsor-funded and outside the marketing budget. Hall-4 seats 8,000 theatre-style and hosts the indoor pro-nite. Halls 1-3 (2,500 each) take competitions and workshops, and the Lawn holds 2,800 [VEN HYD-16]. Demand, using the 2025 day pattern (Day-1 uniques = 1,430 / 2,050 = 69.8%; Day 2 = 65.6%; both days = 35.4%): base gives 1,975 on Day 1, 1,858 on Day 2 and 1,001 on both. Stretch gives 2,462, 2,316 and 1,248. Peak concurrency (ASSUMPTION: at most 65% of a day's uniques on site at the evening peak, plus ~1,000 host students, crew, performers and participants) is 1,284 + 1,000 = ~2,300 in base and 1,600 + 1,000 = ~2,600 in stretch. Permission: apply on the Cyberabad CPPMS portal for a 5,000 peak (about 1.9x the stretch peak). Because the Rs 99 refundable Priority Pass may make the event count as 'ticketed', we treat it that way: the Commissioner approves, with at least 14 days' notice [VEN HYD-26]. We file by 22 Jan, seven weeks out. The stretch case fits inside the same permit and venue, so ambition never trades against safety. Safety rules: QR-only entry, a hard gate cap at the permitted figure, walk-ins registered at the gate counting against that cap, and overbooking only in capped zones, sized as capacity / forecast show-up (e.g. a 1,500-seat front zone / 0.80 = 1,875 priority holders [SHOW-21]). This responds to Mood Indigo 2025 [FEST NAT-01] and Malla Reddy 2026 (about 7,000 permitted, about 20,000 came) [FEST HYD-13]. Gates: the 2025 peak was 251 first entries per hour on Day 1 (17.6% of Day-1 uniques), which scales to 347/hr in base and 432/hr in stretch. Four QR lanes at 240-360 scans per hour each (ASSUMPTION) handle about 1,000-1,400/hr. Target manual admissions under 3% (2025: 9.4%) and pre-validate passes (2025: 50 denied, 30 pending). Exit: the pro-nite ends at 9:45 pm, before the 10 pm outdoor sound rule [VEN HYD-27]. A last-mile loop to HITEC City station (2.6 km [VEN HYD-15]) runs 9:45-10:45 pm for the 11 pm last train [VEN HYD-11]; it is an ops cost, not marketing. We also ask HMRL for an extension, citing its NYE and IPL precedents [VEN HYD-12]. March afternoons average 35.2°C [VEN HYD-10], so crowd-heavy sessions run from 4 pm.

framework.name: ICE (Impact, Confidence, Ease; Sean Ellis) on anchored 1-10 scales, averaged as (I+C+E)/3 [GRO-03]. Ties are broken first by rupees per incremental verified visitor, then by dependency order (the shared rail ranks first). Separately, any idea asking for incremental money has to beat the marginal cost per visitor of our best scalable channel (partners, Rs 128). Tests under Rs 10k are exempt because they buy information.
framework.how_scored: Impact is anchored to base incremental visitors: 10 = 500 or more; 8 = 300-499; 6 = 150-299; 4 = 75-149; 2 = under 75. Confidence is anchored to evidence tier: 10 = our 2025 data on this exact mechanism; 8 = our data on the same channel or proxy, or several RCTs of the same mechanism; 6 = one external RCT or benchmark; 4 = an observational correlation only; 2 = assumption only. Ease is anchored to cash, team time and outside approvals: 10 = Rs 10k or less, 5 person-weeks or less, no approvals; 7 = Rs 35k or less, 8 person-weeks or less, internal build; 4 = more than Rs 1L, or more than 20 person-weeks, or many outside approvals. Results: #1 Engine 4/8/10 = 7.33; #2 Clusters 10/8/4 = 7.33 (tie broken: Rs 98 vs Rs 128 per incremental visitor, and #3-#5 depend on #1); #3 Squads 8/6/7 = 7.00; #4 Leak-proof 4/8/9 = 7.00 (tie broken on absolute impact, 310 vs 77); #5 Ladder 2/4/7 = 4.33. Team capacity is ~75 person-weeks (5 owners x 15 weeks), allocated as: Engine 5, Clusters 25, Squads 8, Leak-proof 4, Ladder 6, always-on paid 6, dashboard and analysis 10, permissions and ops 8. We double down on #1 and #2 (plus #3 once k is at least 0.30). #4 is a no-regret configuration. #5 is a test.

ideas.name: Reserved-for-You Show-up Engine (WhatsApp commitment, plan-making, reminder cadence)
ideas.concept: Every registrant gets the pass on WhatsApp worded as ownership: 'Your spot is reserved: Day 1, Gate B'. A 3-tap plan-making prompt asks when they will arrive, which route they will take (metro station, college bus, own vehicle) and who they are coming with. A 4-touch cadence follows. T-7: reconfirm, with a loss-framed option to release the spot to someone on the waitlist. T-2: route card with last-train information. T-1: reminder. Morning-of: gate and QR. Anyone who registered more than 30 days out gets an extra T-30 reconfirm. This replaces the generic nurture email. A randomised 15% holdout gets only the pass and one day-before logistics message.
ideas.why_it_works: In 2025, 575 confirmed registrants did not come and there was no reminder cadence. The single nurture email had zero lift (69.0% vs 68.7%) and 12.7% of recipients opted out. Confirmed registrants who signed up 31-60 days out attended at only 72.1%, against 80.5-81.6% for 0-30 days. External trials: SMS reminders cut no-shows 25% (RR 0.75) [SHOW-09]; reminders 3 days and 1 day before beat either alone [SHOW-10]; 'reserved for you' ownership wording worked best [SHOW-13]; making a plan raised turnout 4.1 points, and 9.1 points for people deciding alone [SHOW-14]; loss or cost framing cut missed appointments 23-34% [SHOW-11/12]. A utility message costs about Rs 0.115 [WA-01].
ideas.contribution_math: This is applied to the confirmed pool after idea 4, so it cannot double count. Base: 3,135 confirmed x 19.1% residual no-show x 20% cut x 85% treated = +102. Stretch: 3,691 x 18.3% x 30% x 85% = +172. The holdout costs about 18 visitors in base (3,135 x 19.1% x 20% x 15%); that is the price of proving the lift. Rs 10,000 / 102 = Rs 98 per incremental visitor.
ideas.resources: One CRM/ops owner at about 0.3 FTE (~5 person-weeks; the same person runs idea 4) and one volunteer writing English and Telugu templates. Tools: a WhatsApp BSP (about Rs 1,000 a month [WA-04]) plus Luma or KonfHub for registration and QR passes [SHOW-23/24]. Cash: ~21,700 utility messages x ~Rs 0.24 all-in ≈ Rs 5,200, platform Rs 4,000, buffer Rs 800.
ideas.timeline: 26 Nov - 20 Dec: onboard the BSP, get Meta template approval, build the holdout randomiser. Goes live with registration on Mon 4 Jan. The January pre-fest workshops are the first test beds, read at Gate 1 (18 Jan). T-30 reconfirms start 11 Feb. Show-up week: T-7 on Sat 6 Mar; T-2 on Thu 11 Mar (moved off Eid on ~10 Mar); T-1 on Fri 12 Mar; morning-of on 13 and 14 Mar. Holdout readout by 21 Mar.
ideas.test_design: A randomised 85/15 holdout, assigned by phone-number hash and stratified by source channel, runs for the whole campaign. Primary metric: check-in rate of confirmed registrants. With about 470 people in the holdout, the minimum detectable effect is about 5 points at 80% power, so a 3-4 point effect will read as directional; we pre-register that. Inside the treated group, we A/B the T-7 wording ('your spot is reserved' ownership vs 'release it for someone on the waitlist' loss framing) on YES-reply rate, with about 1,330 per arm, enough to detect about 5 points. For an early read, 6-8 pre-fest club workshops in January run a 50/50 reminder vs no-reminder split (directional).
kpis: WhatsApp opt-in at registration: 90% or more
Delivery rate: 95% or more
Plan-making completion: 50% or more
T-7 YES-reply: 75% or more overall, and no channel under 60%
Opt-out or block rate: 3% or less
Check-in gap between treated and holdout: 3 points or more
Rupees per incremental visitor: Rs 100 or less
ideas.framework_scores: ICE: Impact 4 (102 visitors); Confidence 8 (three RCTs of the same mechanism [SHOW-09/10/14], 2025 had no cadence, and its one email had zero lift); Ease 10 (Rs 10k, ~5 person-weeks, only Meta template approval needed). Score 7.33. It ties with #2 and ranks first because it costs Rs 98 vs Rs 128 per incremental visitor and ideas #3-#5 run on its WhatsApp rail.
ideas.dependencies_risks_overlap: Depends on Meta template approval and on WhatsApp opt-in at registration. Risks: message fatigue lowering the Meta quality rating; Eid falling at T-3; first-year mid-terms (3-9 Mar) during show-up week; Telugu and English copy quality. Overlap with #4 (same rail) is removed by sequence: #4 acts only on people without a live pass, #1 only on people with one. #3 and #5 effects are computed on the no-shows that remain after #1.
ideas.critical_variables: WhatsApp opt-in rate; delivery and read rates; plan-making completion; T-7 YES-reply rate (the leading indicator of check-in, tracked by channel); opt-out rate and Meta quality rating; timing around Eid and first-year mid-terms.
ideas.early_success_signal: Gate 1 (18 Jan): the reminded arm of the pre-fest workshops checks in 5 points or more above control; plan-making completion is 50% or more; opt-out is 3% or less; delivery is 95% or more. Gate 3 (22 Feb): 80% or more of early registrants reply YES to the T-30 reconfirm.
ideas.early_failure_signal: Opt-out above 5% in any week, or the Meta quality rating drops to 'low'. Plan-making completion under 30%. The reminded workshop arm is no better than control. T-7 YES under 60% in any source channel.
ideas.scale_threshold: If the pre-fest gap is 5 points or more and opt-out is 3% or less at Gate 1: add the T-30 reconfirm for everyone registered more than 30 days out, and add Telugu variants. The holdout stays at 15%. Here we scale coverage, not cash.
ideas.change_threshold: If opt-out is 3-5%, or plan-making completion is 30-40%: drop to 3 touches (cut T-30), shrink the plan prompt to one tap, and move all T-7 sends to whichever wording wins after 500 sends per arm.
ideas.stop_threshold: If opt-out exceeds 8%, or the quality rating stays 'low' for 3 days: stop every non-utility send. Keep only the pass and the T-1 logistics message, with SMS or email as fallback [SMS-01].
ideas.action_on_change: When a channel's T-7 YES rate is under 60% (CTWA is the likely case): release its non-responders' passes to the waitlist (handed to #4), nudge their squad leads (#3), and lower that channel's show-up forecast in the capacity model before the next waitlist batch.
ideas.dashboard_ai_support: Dashboard: a reminder cohort table (sent, delivered, read and replied, by touch and channel), a check-in forecast for treated vs holdout, and an opt-out alarm. The AI copilot runs tools on live Neon data. Asked 'which channel has the weakest T-7 reconfirm this week?', it computes the gap against the threshold and drafts a release-batch or template-swap task, which is written only after a human approves it. Until the holdout readout exists, it says so ('holdout n = 470; lift not yet measurable') instead of claiming lift.

ideas.name: Campus Cluster Partnerships run by check-in-paid ambassadors (plus a partner-bus pilot)
ideas.concept: Geocode the 107 metro engineering colleges and the top degree colleges into 5 clusters. Example clusters, to be checked by geocoding: Medchal-Maisammaguda (N), Bachupally-Miyapur (NW), Gandipet-Gachibowli (W), Ghatkesar-Uppal (E), Ibrahimpatnam-LB Nagar (SE). Sign 40 in-kind MOUs: pass quotas for clubs, showcase slots, co-branded pre-fest AI/GCC workshops and certificates, with no paid stalls. 45 ambassadors cover the non-partner colleges and are paid per verified check-in, not per registration: Rs 50 each plus tiered non-cash rewards (pass, certificate, recommendation letter, front zone for the top 10). Every partner gets a weekly cadence so none goes idle. Pilot: 2 college-owned buses lent by partners in the two farthest clusters run on Day 1, with us paying fuel and driver only, and only if at least 40 seats are booked.
ideas.why_it_works: College partnerships were 2025's best channel: 90.0% of identified people registered, 85.6% of registrants attended, cancellations were 4.0% and cost was Rs 81 per visitor. Yet the channel got 11.3% of spend and sat idle for about 3 weeks (registrations went 21, 8, 0 in weeks 8-10, and spend postings skipped 4-28 Feb). Hyderabad is dense: 465 + 338 colleges in two districts [MKT HYD-04], an average private engineering college of about 675 freshers a year [MKT HYD-08], and 132 IEEE branches [MED-18]. 70% of Indian Gen Z attend events with friends or in groups [MED-25]. National fests grow on tiered, mostly non-cash ambassador rewards [CA-01, FEST NAT-05].
ideas.contribution_math: Registrations = spend / CPR, using the 2025 CPR up to each channel's 2025 spend and 1.25x above it, with registrants above 2025 volume showing up 10 points less. Partners, Rs 90k: 31,000/68.9 = 450 registrations x 85.6% = 385 visitors, plus 59,000/86.1 = 685 x 75.6% = 518. Total 903 visitors, +518 vs 2025. Clubs, Rs 20k: 200 x 82.5% + 40 x 72.5% = 194, +29. Ambassadors held at Rs 42k: 520 x 75% = 390, +0, no increment claimed. Bus pilot: 85 riders x 14.3% residual no-show x 50% = +6. Base total: +553. Stretch (1.10x CPR, 5-point drop): partners 1,012 (+627), clubs 200 (+35), 4 bus-days +9, total +671. The extra Rs 71k over 2025's cluster spend / 553 = Rs 128 per incremental visitor.
ideas.resources: A full-time partnerships owner (~15 person-weeks), the growth lead running the MOU tracker (~2 person-weeks), 5 volunteer cluster leads (~8 person-weeks) and 45 ambassadors: about 25 core person-weeks. Cash: activation Rs 90k (about Rs 2,250 per partner for workshop logistics, print and club merch; the last Rs 30k is gated); ambassadors Rs 42k; clubs and community Rs 20k; bus pilot Rs 8k (2 bus-days x Rs 4,000).
ideas.timeline: 26 Nov - 20 Dec: geocode, shortlist 60 colleges, pair and randomise them into waves. 20 MOUs by Wed 6 Jan, before Sankranti (13-17 Jan). Wave-1 workshops 4-24 Jan. 40 MOUs by 31 Jan. No activations 1-6 Feb (mid-terms). Sprint 8 Feb - 5 Mar with a weekly per-partner cadence. Bus go/no-go Wed 3 Mar (T-10).
ideas.test_design: A matched-pair staggered rollout. Pair the 60 shortlisted colleges by size and cluster, and randomly put one of each pair in wave 1 (Dec-Jan) and the other in wave 2 (Feb). At Gate 2, registrations per 1,000 students in wave-1 colleges vs not-yet-active wave-2 colleges give the causal lift from partnering, net of spill-over from paid and organic. Ambassador incentive A/B: randomise ambassadors to pay-per-verified-check-in vs pay-per-registration (both capped) and compare their recruits' T-7 reconfirm and check-in rates. Bus pilot: compare booked riders with non-riders from the same cluster. This also measures Hyderabad's distance penalty, which the 2025 data cannot.
kpis: MOUs: 20 by 6 Jan, 40 by 31 Jan
Registrations per partner per week during the sprint: 8 or more
Partners with no registration in 7 days: 0
CPR above 2025 spend level: Rs 86 or less
Live-pass share among partner registrants: 94% or more
Check-in rate of partner-sourced registrants: 80% or more
Cost per visitor for the cluster channels: Rs 110 or less
Bus: at least 40 bookings per bus, and rider check-in of 90% or more
ideas.framework_scores: ICE: Impact 10 (553 visitors); Confidence 8 (our own 2025 data on the same channel; the uncertainty is about scaling it); Ease 4 (Rs 1.6L, ~25 person-weeks, 40 outside approvals, a busy exam calendar). Score 7.33. Ranked #2 on the tie-break: Rs 128 vs Rs 98 per incremental visitor, and it ramps up by week 8 where #1 is live by week 2.
ideas.dependencies_risks_overlap: Needs #1 live before the first workshop, and the programme published by 4 Jan. Depends on college admin approvals and the calendar: Sankranti, mid-terms 1-6 Feb, GATE weekends 6-21 Feb, Ramadan from about 9 Feb. Risks: a repeat of 2025's stall; ambassadors inflating sign-ups, which is neutralised by paying only on verified check-ins with one phone per QR; newly added colleges converting worse, which is already priced in through the 1.25x CPR and the 10-point drop. Overlap with #3 (same campuses): phone dedupe and first-touch codes. Ambassadors work only non-partner colleges, and their budget stays at the 2025 level, so no ambassador increment is claimed.
ideas.critical_variables: Speed of signing MOUs; registrations per partner per week; number of idle partners; CPR above the 2025 spend level; reconfirm rate of wave-2 registrants (the quality of the extra volume); share of ambassadors who are active; bus seat bookings per route.
ideas.early_success_signal: 20 or more MOUs by 6 Jan. Wave-1 workshops average 60 or more attendees. At Gate 2, wave-1 colleges have at least 2x the registrations per 1,000 students of wave-2 colleges. CPR above the 2025 spend level is Rs 86 or less. 35 or more of the 45 ambassadors have at least one registration by Gate 1.
ideas.early_failure_signal: Fewer than 12 MOUs by 6 Jan. Three or more partners with no registrations for 7 days, which is the 2025 week-10 stall pattern. CPR above Rs 110 at Gate 2. Wave-1 colleges no better than wave-2.
ideas.scale_threshold: At Gate 2, if CPR is Rs 86 or less and partner registrants' live-pass share is 94% or more: release the Rs 16k contingency to 5 wave-3 partners (about 185 registrations at Rs 86). For buses: if there are at least 40 bookings per bus at T-10 and rider check-in reaches 90% or more on Day 1, add Day-2 bus-days from the contingency.
ideas.change_threshold: If CPR is Rs 86-110, or any partner is idle for more than 7 days: switch the activation format (circular to a club-run event plus a squad drive), reassign the ambassador, and move ambassadors from the lowest-yield cluster to the highest.
ideas.stop_threshold: Per partner: fewer than 10 registrations after 3 active weeks means drop it and replace it from the shortlist. Programme-wide: if forecast cost per visitor exceeds Rs 150 at Gate 3, freeze the remaining activation tranche and move it to squads. Bus: fewer than 40 bookings at T-10 means cancel, at no cost.
ideas.action_on_change: If any cluster's weekly registrations fall more than 40% with spend flat (the 2025 stall pattern), its cluster lead gets a same-day call list, the paid geo-fence shifts to that cluster for one week, and the partnerships owner reviews it at the next weekly standup.
ideas.dashboard_ai_support: Dashboard: a partner and cluster leaderboard (registrations, live-pass share, reconfirm rate, cost per visitor), an MOU pipeline, an idle-partner alert after 5 days, and a wave-1 vs wave-2 test panel. The copilot answers 'which partners went quiet this week, and what did they deliver before?' from live data, computes CPR against the Rs 86 threshold, and proposes follow-up tasks with an owner and deadline that are created only after approval. Asked about distance effects, it says the data cannot answer until the geocoded college table exists.

ideas.name: Squad Passes (register as a group, see each other check in, get rewarded only when everyone arrives)
ideas.concept: Step 2 of registration asks 'Who's coming with you?' A squad of 3-6 shares one squad link, but every member still gets their own QR so the unique-visitor count stays clean. Squad leads see progress ('3 of 4 confirmed'). On site, members can see each other's check-ins, and a live inter-college squad leaderboard runs on screens and WhatsApp. Rewards are paid only when the whole squad is verified on arrival: a fast lane plus a Rs 100 food combo, and front-zone pro-nite access for the top 3 colleges. This replaces the 2025 referral link.
ideas.why_it_works: 2025 referrals were the cheapest channel: Rs 69 per visitor and 78.6% show-up. 70% of Indian Gen Z attend events with friends [MED-25]. Showing people that neighbours could see their turnout raised turnout 8.1 points [SHOW-15]. Plan-making helps most for people deciding alone [SHOW-14], and a squad turns a solo decision into a group one. Benchmarks: the median share of customers who refer is about 19% [REF-01], and referral programmes lift festival ticket income 20-30% [REF-02].
ideas.contribution_math: k (net-new friends per seed registrant) = 19% of the 2,578 seed registrants start a squad (the Extole median [REF-01]) x 2.6 friends each (squads of 3-4) x 60% net-new = 0.296, so 764 net-new registrations. The 510 friends assumed to come anyway are excluded. Visitors: the first 350 show up at the 2025 referral rate of 78.6% = 275, and the next 414 at 68.6% = 284. That is 559 visitors, +284 over the 275 that 2025 referrals produced. Social visibility: squad members (1,764 people, 53% of registrants) get a further 10% cut in residual no-show = +26. Base total: +310. Stretch: 25% of seeds start squads, so k = 0.39 = 1,080 registrations and 812 visitors (+537), a 20% visibility effect (+65) and 75 more gate walk-ins from squad add-ons, total +677. The extra Rs 16k over 2025's referral budget / 310 = Rs 52 per incremental visitor.
ideas.resources: A community/referral owner (~8 person-weeks); in 2025 the referral owner had the lowest cost per visitor (Rs 69). Ambassadors double as squad captains. One volunteer developer builds the squad link. Cash: about 245 complete squads x Rs 100 = Rs 24,500 (assuming half of about 490 squads arrive complete), leaderboard prizes and signage Rs 5,500, squad-link build Rs 5,000.
ideas.timeline: Build 1-31 Dec. A/B 4-24 Jan, read at Gate 1 (18 Jan). Full rollout by 25 Jan. Leaderboard live 8 Feb - 14 Mar. Rewards handed out at the gate on 13-14 Mar.
ideas.test_design: For the first three weeks, landing-page sessions are randomised 50/50: squad-first registration vs solo-first with a 2025-style referral link. Primary metric: k, measured as net-new registrations per seed registrant within 7 days (the median gap between first contact and registration). The target is 0.30 or more, against 0.14 in 2025 (350 / 2,450). Guardrail: registration completion falls by no more than 2 points. On event day, compare squad vs solo check-in rates within the same source channel.
kpis: Squad formation: 19% or more of seed registrants
Friends per squad lead: 2.6 or more
k: 0.30 or more
Registration completion: no more than 2 points below control
Squads fully confirmed at T-7: 60% or more
Squads that arrive complete: 50% or more
Check-in gap, squad members vs solo: 3 points or more
Rupees per net-new visitor: Rs 70 or less
ideas.framework_scores: ICE: Impact 8 (310 visitors); Confidence 6 (our own referral data on cost and show-up, but the visibility RCT comes from voting and k is an assumption); Ease 7 (Rs 35k, ~8 person-weeks, internal build). Score 7.00. Ranked above #4 on absolute impact (310 vs 77).
ideas.dependencies_risks_overlap: Runs on #1's WhatsApp rail and uses #2's ambassadors as captains. k is the most sensitive assumption in the whole plan: if 10% of seeds start squads instead of 19%, base falls by 288 visitors. Fake squads are prevented by paying rewards only on verified check-in, with one phone per member. A squad lead dropping out could pull friends out too, so we watch whether no-shows cluster by squad. Squads arriving together create gate surges, so they get a dedicated lane. Overlap with #2: the 40% of friends who would have come anyway are excluded, and phones are deduplicated.
ideas.critical_variables: Squad formation rate; friends per lead; net-new share (each friend's first-touch code vs existing registrations); drop in registration completion; whether no-shows cluster within squads.
ideas.early_success_signal: By Gate 1 the A/B shows k of 0.30 or more in the squad-first arm vs about 0.14 in control, completion down no more than 2 points, and average squad size of 3.4 or more.
ideas.early_failure_signal: k below 0.15, no better than the 2025 link. Completion down more than 5 points. More than 30% of squads still have only one member after 7 days.
ideas.scale_threshold: If k is 0.30 or more at Gate 1, make squad-first the flow for everyone. At Gate 2, if cost per net-new visitor is Rs 70 or less, add Rs 8k from contingency for college leaderboard prizes and ambassador-run squad drives in the top 2 clusters.
ideas.change_threshold: If k is 0.15-0.30: lower the minimum squad size from 4 to 3, make the step skippable, switch the reward from food to front-zone access, and prefill friends from the 'who with' answer in plan-making.
ideas.stop_threshold: If k is below 0.15 at Gate 2: revert to a plain referral link and move the roughly Rs 20k of unspent rewards to partner wave 3.
ideas.action_on_change: At T-7, squads with unconfirmed members get a lead-targeted nudge ('2 of your 4 haven't confirmed'). Squads still incomplete at T-3 can transfer the unconfirmed members' passes to new friends; this is handed to #4.
ideas.dashboard_ai_support: Dashboard: a squad funnel (formed, partial, fully confirmed, arrived), k by cluster and week, and a list of incomplete squads by college. Asked 'how many Ghatkesar squads are missing members?', the copilot computes it from live data, drafts a nudge task that needs approval, and flags when k drops below 0.30.

ideas.name: Leak-proof Capacity (manage passes like airline seats)
ideas.concept: Five changes. (1) Instant auto-confirm with a QR pass, so there is no 'interested' limbo: in 2025 the median wait was 2.1 days and 29 people never confirmed. (2) Overbook each capped zone by capacity / forecast show-up. (3) Backfill the waitlist automatically in batches at T-7, T-3 and T-1: in 2025, 88 waitlisted people never got in. (4) Replace a plain 'cancel' with 'Can't make it?', offering a switch of day, a transfer to a friend or a release. (5) Send cancellers a win-back message at T-3: in 2025, 36 of 219 cancellers reconfirmed.
ideas.why_it_works: Pass status is the strongest show-up predictor in the data: confirmed registrants attended at 77%, while cancelled, waitlisted and 'interested' registrants attended at 0%. That was 300 of 2,800 registrants (10.7%) who could not attend under any circumstances. The airline-style rule 'accept capacity / expected show rate' [SHOW-21, SHOW-22] turns no-shows into seats for people on the waitlist.
ideas.contribution_math: Leakage in the base mix = 26.5% no-show x 34.3% (2025: 300 of 875 non-attending registrants never reached a live pass) = 9.08% of 3,343 = 304 people. Recover 80% of 'interested' (9.7% of leakers), 60% of the waitlisted (29.3%) and 10% of cancellations (61.0%): 31.4% of leakers, or 95 more live passes. At the 80.9% confirmed show-up rate, that is +77. Stretch: recover 100% / 85% / 30% = 52.9% of 335 = 177 people x 81.7% = +145. Rs 5,000 / 77 = Rs 65 per incremental visitor.
ideas.resources: The same CRM/ops owner as #1 (~4 person-weeks). The growth lead owns the show-up forecast model (~2 person-weeks). Two volunteers staff the gate exception desk. Cash: about 4,000 marketing-category messages (waitlist offers and win-backs) x ~Rs 1.1 all-in (Rs 0.8631 [WA-01] + GST + BSP) ≈ Rs 4,400, plus a Rs 600 buffer. Auto-confirm, transfer and waitlist are configuration in the registration tool [SHOW-24].
ideas.timeline: Rules configured by 3 Jan (auto-confirm, transfer, switch-day). Overbooking ratios set at Gate 2 (8 Feb) from pre-fest data, then recalibrated weekly. Waitlist batches at T-7 (6 Mar), T-3 and T-1 (12 Mar). Win-back at T-3. The Day-2 batch is sized from Day-1 gate counts.
ideas.test_design: Randomise the cancellation flow 50/50: 'switch day / transfer to a friend / release' vs a plain cancel. Primary metric: passes saved (kept, switched or transferred) per cancel request. The release rule is pre-registered: batch size = (zone capacity - forecast check-ins) x 0.9. Forecast error is scored by zone after each pre-fest event and after Day 1.
kpis: Live pass within 48 h of registering: 95% or more (2025 median: 2.1 days)
Waitlist at T-1: 20 or fewer (2025: 88 never admitted)
Final cancellation rate: 5% or less (2025: 6.5%)
Save rate on cancel requests: 25% or more (2025 win-back: 16.4%)
Forecast error by zone: within ±5%
Forecast peak vs permit: 90% or less
ideas.framework_scores: ICE: Impact 4 (77 visitors); Confidence 8 (exact 2025 leakage counts and a measured 16% win-back); Ease 9 (Rs 5k, ~4 person-weeks, configuration rather than build). Score 7.00. Ranked below #3 on absolute impact.
ideas.dependencies_risks_overlap: Shares #1's rail and depends on an accurate show-up forecast and on the police-permitted number. Its biggest risk is the opposite of leakage: overbooking past the permit. Malla Reddy in 2026 had permission for about 7,000 people and about 20,000 came [FEST HYD-13]; Mood Indigo 2025 had to shut outsiders out [FEST NAT-01]. Hence a hard gate cap and QR-only entry. Overlap with #1 is removed by sequence: #4 acts only on people without a live pass and is applied first.
ideas.critical_variables: Show-up forecast by zone and day; cancellation rate; waitlist size; save rate; headroom under the permit.
ideas.early_success_signal: At Gate 2: 95% or more get a live pass within 48 h, the new cancellation flow saves 25% or more, and pre-fest forecast error is within 5%.
ideas.early_failure_signal: Cancellations above 7% of registrants by Gate 3. Forecast error above 10%. More than 100 people still waitlisted at T-7.
ideas.scale_threshold: If the T-7 forecast puts a zone at 85% of capacity or less: raise its acceptance ratio from capacity / 0.80 to capacity / 0.75 and release a larger waitlist batch.
ideas.change_threshold: If the save rate is below 15%: rewrite the offer, making 'transfer to your squad' the default. If forecast error is above 10%: recalibrate by source channel and registration lead time (registrants 31-60 days out attended at 72.1%).
ideas.stop_threshold: If the forecast peak reaches 90% of permitted concurrency: stop overbooking, close new registrations for that zone and run a waitlist only. If the Day-1 gate count came within 10% of the cap, withhold the Day-2 batch.
ideas.action_on_change: As soon as a channel's reconfirm rate falls (a signal from #1), its forecast show-up is lowered and the freed seats go into the next waitlist batch the same day.
ideas.dashboard_ai_support: Dashboard: a status funnel (interested, live, waitlisted, cancelled, transferred), a waitlist burn-down chart, and a zone capacity forecast against the permit for each day. Asked 'how many waitlisted people can we release for the Day-1 pro-nite?', the copilot computes capacity / forecast show-up from live data, shows its arithmetic and creates the release task only after approval. It warns when headroom under the permit falls below 10%.

ideas.name: Commitment Ladder ('Build your fest' session picks plus a Rs 99 refundable Priority Pass test)
ideas.concept: After registering, students pick two or more sessions: AI/GCC workshops, hackathon or BGMI team slots, competitions. Their seats are held until a set time, and they are invited to send one question to a speaker. A randomised half of registrants is also offered an opt-in Rs 99 refundable Priority Pass for the pro-nite front zone. The Rs 99 comes back as food or merch credit at check-in, so it costs nothing net, and deposits forfeited by no-shows fund squad rewards.
ideas.why_it_works: These are the two strongest behavioural signals in our data, though both are observational. In 2025, registrants who downloaded the programme attended at 74.7% vs 61.9%, and those who submitted a question attended at 79.4% vs 68.0%. External evidence: paid events have about 11 points fewer no-shows than free ones [SHOW-01], but within the same event, personally paying adds only 2-4 points [SHOW-04]. One case, Basecamp, saw no-shows fall from 55% to 10% with a deposit [SHOW-08]. 72% of engineering seats are CSE or allied [MKT HYD-09], so tech sessions are the right commitment hook.
ideas.contribution_math: This acts on the no-shows left after #1 and #3: 15.0% of the 3,135 confirmed. 40% of registrants pick sessions, which cuts their no-show by 25% (about a third of the 12.8-point observational gap for programme downloads). Coverage is 80% because of the 50/50 test until Gate 2. 3,135 x 15.0% x 0.40 x 0.25 x 0.80 = +38. Stretch: 55% pick sessions with a 35% cut = +67. Rs 5,000 / 38 = Rs 132 per incremental visitor. That is above the Rs 128 bar for scaling money, so it stays a test until it proves causal.
ideas.resources: A programme/content owner (~6 person-weeks) and one volunteer for the session catalogue. Workshop hosts come from GCC and tech sponsors, on the sponsor side of the budget. Cash: gateway fees on about 400 deposits (~Rs 1,500 [SHOW-23]), seat-hold cards and print Rs 2,000, speaker-question prompts and recaps Rs 1,500.
ideas.timeline: Session catalogue and deposit flow go live with registration on 4 Jan. The randomised test runs 4 Jan - 8 Feb, with the rollout decision at Gate 2. Held seats are released to the waitlist at T-3. Deposits are refunded as credit at the gate on 13-14 Mar.
ideas.test_design: A randomised encouragement design. Until Gate 2 (about 1,340 registrations), half of registrants get the 'build your fest' prompt and the Priority Pass offer, and half get a plain confirmation with a brochure link. Intent-to-treat comparisons of T-7 YES-reply and check-in separate cause from the 2025 correlation. Guardrail for the deposit: registration completion, offered vs not offered. Depositor no-shows are compared with people who were offered the pass and declined.
kpis: Share of registrants picking sessions: 40% or more
Sessions per picker: 2 or more
Use of held seats: 80% or more
Deposit opt-in: 15% or more of those offered
Registration completion drop: 3 points or less
T-7 reply gap, encouraged vs control (intent-to-treat): 3 points or more
Depositor no-show: 12% or less
ideas.framework_scores: ICE: Impact 2 (38 visitors); Confidence 4 (an observational correlation in our own data; deposit evidence is thin [SHOW-04/08]); Ease 7 (Rs 5k, ~6 person-weeks, needs sponsor sessions published early). Score 4.33. It stays at #5 because it is cheap and it tells us whether our two best show-up predictors can be pulled as levers or are just markers of intent.
ideas.dependencies_risks_overlap: Depends on sponsors and production publishing the programme by 4 Jan, and on #1 for delivery. Risks: the deposit may put people off registering. A refundable paid pass may make the event 'ticketed', which changes the approving authority and needs at least 14 days' notice [VEN HYD-26]; we file 7 weeks out regardless. Held seats could block real attendees, so they are released at T-3. Overlap is removed by applying this only to the no-shows left after #1 and #3.
ideas.critical_variables: Share of registrants picking sessions; the causal (intent-to-treat) gap; deposit opt-in against the completion drop; no-show among held seats.
ideas.early_success_signal: At Gate 2: the encouraged arm's T-30 or T-7 YES-reply is 3 points or more above control; 40% or more pick sessions; deposit opt-in is 15% or more with completion down no more than 3 points.
ideas.early_failure_signal: Fewer than 20% pick sessions. The intent-to-treat gap is zero or negative. The deposit cuts completion by more than 5 points.
ideas.scale_threshold: If the intent-to-treat gap is 3 points or more at Gate 2: show the prompt to every new registrant, and leave the existing control arm untouched until the event so the check-in comparison stays clean.
ideas.change_threshold: If deposit opt-in is below 10%: cut the deposit to Rs 49 or make it a squad-level deposit. If fewer than 30% pick sessions: trim the catalogue to the top 10 sessions and preselect by branch.
ideas.stop_threshold: If the deposit cuts completion by more than 5 points: drop the deposit and keep free session picks. If the intent-to-treat gap is zero or negative with at least 1,000 people: stop prompting, and stop using brochure downloads as an input to the show-up forecast.
ideas.action_on_change: At T-3, unclaimed held seats go to waitlisted people who picked that session (handed to #4). Depositors who have not reconfirmed by T-7 get a personal 'your Rs 99 credit is waiting' message.
ideas.dashboard_ai_support: Dashboard: a picker vs control cohort panel (reply rate, forecast show-up), a deposit funnel, and held-seat use by session. The copilot keeps correlation and causation apart. For example: 'In 2025, brochure downloaders attended 12.8 points more often, but that is observational. The randomised gap so far is X with n = Y.' At T-3 it drafts a 'release held seats' task for approval.

drafts.overlap_adjustment: Attribution is a fixed-order waterfall starting from the 2025 actual of 2,050, so each visitor is counted once. Six rules: (1) Acquisition ideas (#2 and #3) get credit only for registrations above each channel's 2025 volume. Those registrants are valued at 2025 channel show-up rates minus a 10-point quality drop, before any new conversion mechanic. Ambassadors are held at their 2025 budget, so no ambassador increment is claimed. (2) Squads count only 60% of invited friends as net-new. The other 40%, 510 registrations in base, are assumed to come anyway through the same colleges. Every registration is deduplicated by phone, with first-touch codes. (3) Conversion ideas act one after another on the remaining no-shows, in a declared order: #4 (people without a live pass) first, then #1 (confirmed people, 85% treated), then #3's visibility effect (squad members), then #5 (session pickers, 80% coverage), then the bus pilot (riders). A person rescued by one idea cannot be rescued again. Computed standalone, these effects would sum to 261 in base and 506 in stretch. Computed in sequence they sum to 249 and 458, so 12 and 48 double-counted visitors are removed. (4) The cut to paid is shown as an explicit negative: -298 in base, -252 in stretch. The five ideas' gross +1,080 is therefore never presented as net growth. (5) Base: 2,050 - 298 + 102 (#1) + 553 (#2) + 310 (#3) + 77 (#4) + 38 (#5) = 2,832. (6) Stretch: 2,050 - 252 + 172 + 671 + 677 (including +75 gate walk-ins credited to squads) + 145 + 67 = 3,530. The contingency (Rs 16k) is not credited in base.

deprioritized.idea: Paid social and creators at 2025 scale (Rs 1.52L): cut 64% to Rs 55k and rebuilt
deprioritized.reason: In 2025 they took 55.4% of spend for 25.1% of visitors, at Rs 274 and Rs 337 per visitor. Only 50% of their registrants attended, opt-out was 12.2% and paid social's CTR was 2.1%. Paid social burned out after week 9: registrations fell from 110-124 a week to 35 with spend flat at Rs 14,400. What remains is rebuilt as Click-to-WhatsApp Reels geo-fenced to the 5 clusters (Reels CPM is about a third of Feed [PAID-01], and a CTWA chat opens a free 7-day messaging window [WA-03]) plus Hyderabad nano creators, with creative rotated every 10-14 days. The trade-off is explicit: we give up 298 low-show visitors from paid to buy 553 from clusters and 310 from squads. Rs 20k of conversion (ideas 1, 4 and 5) delivers 217 visitors, about as many as the Rs 55k of rebuilt paid (217). Kill rule: if CTWA CPR exceeds Rs 140 for 2 weeks, or weekly registrations drop 40% with spend flat, rotate creative within 72 h; if there is no recovery within a week, stop and move the rest to partner wave 3.

deprioritized.idea: A macro influencer or celebrity reel
deprioritized.reason: One costs Rs 2-12 lakh per reel [INF-01], which is the whole budget. Regional micro creators get 2-3x the engagement at about a tenth of the cost, and about 1 in 4 creator profiles fail an authenticity check [INF-04]. Rejected.

deprioritized.idea: Generic nurture email
deprioritized.reason: Our own data shows zero lift (69.0% vs 68.7%) and a 12.7% opt-out. Broadcast email in Indian media and entertainment gets about 17% opens and a 2.2% click-to-open rate [EMAIL-01]. Stopped. Email remains only as a triggered fallback for people without WhatsApp.

deprioritized.idea: Blanket hired shuttles from every cluster
deprioritized.reason: At about Rs 9,000 per hired bus-day (ASSUMPTION; we will get 3 quotes) carrying about 42 booked riders whose show-up rises 15-35 points, each extra visitor costs about Rs 600-1,400, against Rs 98 for the engine. The 2025 data has no geography, so the distance penalty is unknown. Replaced by an Rs 8k pilot using buses that partner colleges lend us. The engine's plan-making and last-train messages cover route friction for free.

deprioritized.idea: Paid general entry, or a mandatory deposit for everyone
deprioritized.reason: Free entry is the norm for Hyderabad fests (Elan 2025: 'free entry for everyone' [FEST HYD-03]). Within a single event, people who pay show up only 2-4 points more often [SHOW-04], and a mandatory deposit could cut registrations by an amount nobody has measured. Rejected. The Rs 99 refundable pass survives only as a randomised opt-in test cell (#5).

deprioritized.idea: Paid stalls or sponsorships at other colleges' fests
deprioritized.reason: They cost Rs 15,000 to Rs 2 lakh each [PART-01] for reach without a commitment step. Partnerships run in kind instead (pass quotas, club showcase slots, co-hosted workshops).

deprioritized.idea: Young IT/GCC professionals as a paid segment
deprioritized.reason: The pool is huge (9.39 lakh [MKT HYD-25]). Any real interest would swamp capacity and permission planning and pull the plan away from students. They get an organic pro-nite listing only, with no spend, and are not counted in the base case.

deprioritized.idea: Intermediate (Class 12) students
deprioritized.reason: Their board exams run 24 Feb - 20 Mar 2027 [VEN HYD-08]. Rejected.

deprioritized.idea: Chasing a headliner as the growth lever
deprioritized.reason: This sits outside the marketing budget (sponsor and production). Hyderabad fests recycle the same acts within weeks [FEST HYD-09], so novelty is weak. Star demand creates crowd-safety and permission risk (Malla Reddy 2026 [FEST HYD-13]). We would announce whatever production books early (over a third of Gen Z act as soon as an event is announced [MED-25]), but we do not budget growth on it.

deprioritized.idea: Unapproved posts on r/hyderabad and paid meme-page blasts
deprioritized.reason: Unapproved advertising on r/hyderabad is removed [MED-09], and meme-page rate cards are unpublished and unverifiable. We will ask the moderators for one approved announcement or AMA, at zero cost.

headline_numbers: Base: 2,832 unique verified external visitors (+38% vs 2,050) on the same Rs 3,00,000 marketing cash, at Rs 106 per visitor (2025: Rs 134).
Stretch: 3,530 (+72%) at Rs 85 per visitor, inside the same permit and venue.
Registrant show-up rises from 68.75% to 81.0% in base and 86.5% in stretch. 52% of base growth (408 of 782) comes from people who had already registered.
Registrations go from 2,800 to 3,343 in base (+19%) and 3,849 in stretch. 80% come from partners, clubs, ambassadors and squads, against 54% in 2025.
The trade-off is deliberate: paid social and creators drop from Rs 1.52L to Rs 0.55L (-298 visitors), funding +553 from campus clusters and +310 from squads.
Rs 20k of conversion (engine, leak-proof capacity, commitment ladder) delivers 217 visitors at Rs 92 each. The Rs 55k left in paid delivers the same 217 at Rs 254 each.
Downside floor: about 2,386 (+16%) if CPRs rise 1.5x, the squad loop halves, the engine works at half strength and paid stays at 2025 cost.

Peak on site is about 2,300 in base and 2,600 in stretch, against a 5,000 permit request on the Cyberabad CPPMS portal (filed 22 Jan) and HITEX Hall-4's 8,000 seats. Day-1 first entries peak at 347 an hour (432 in stretch).
Dates: Sat-Sun 13-14 Mar 2027, after mid-terms, GATE and Eid and before Holi and the April exams. Four gates (18 Jan, 8 Feb, 22 Feb, 6 Mar) decide when to scale, change or stop each idea.

drafts.big_idea: Make the verified check-in the unit of growth. Every registrant becomes a squad lead, every club a batch and every ambassador a league player. Rewards fire only when people actually walk through the HITEX gate, and an AI show-up engine closes the 31% no-show gap. Result: 2,932 unique verified external visitors on Rs 3.0L in the base case (+43% on 2025) and 4,484 at stretch (2.2x).
drafts.north_star: Unique verified external visitors (UVEV): distinct external people, deduped on a stable ID (phone + college-ID hash), with at least one admitted AND verified QR check-in on Sat-Sun 13-14 Mar 2027. These are the 2025 counting rules [DS]. Input tree: seed registrations by bet (B1 clubs, B4 ambassadors, B5 reels) x loop multiplier 1/(1-k) from B3 squads x registrant show-up rate (B2, measured against a holdout) + capped walk-ins. Guardrails: cost per verified visitor at or below Rs 105 (base); WhatsApp opt-out at or below 5%; peak on-site at or below 90% of the 5,000 police permission. Registrations are an input metric, never the goal [GRO-01].
city_rationale: Citation key: [DS] = CampusFest 2025 dataset (research/data_findings.md, analysis/out/deep_dive.json). Brief fact IDs repeat across sections, so they carry a section prefix: mkt = hyd-market, fest = fest-landscape, cal = venue-calendar. SHOW, MED, PAID, INF, WA, REF, CA, NAT, GRO, GEM and PART IDs are unique. A# = a labelled assumption.

Tier-1 by policy and cheaper than its peers. Hyderabad (UA) is an X-class city under the 7th CPC HRA order [mkt HYD-24]. Mercer 2024 ranks Hyderabad 202, against Bengaluru 195, Delhi 164 and Mumbai 136 [mkt HYD-27].

Dense student market. Hyderabad district has 465 colleges (4th in India) and Ranga Reddy 338 (9th) [mkt HYD-04]. Telangana has more than 16 lakh higher-education students, about half of them in Hyderabad + Ranga Reddy, so the local pool is about 8 lakh [MED-19]; cross-check: 17.87 lakh statewide [mkt HYD-01]. Telangana's GER is 46.6 against 30.0 nationally [mkt HYD-02]. The base target is 0.37% of that pool, so conversion, not reach, is the constraint.

The clustered engineering belt suits squads, clubs and buses. 107 of 175 engineering colleges are in Medchal-Malkajgiri, Ranga Reddy and Hyderabad [mkt HYD-11]. 83,622 of 1,16,877 seats are in CSE and allied branches [mkt HYD-09], which supports hackathon, AI and gaming hooks. 515 GCCs [mkt HYD-26] and 9.39 lakh IT workers [mkt HYD-25] are a natural pool of sponsors and internship rewards.

Clean date: Sat-Sun 13-14 Mar 2027. It falls after the JNTUH II-IV mid-terms (1-6 Feb) inside the 8 Feb-3 Apr instruction spell [cal HYD-01], after GATE (Feb weekends) [cal HYD-07], after first-year mid-terms (3-9 Mar) [cal HYD-02] and after Eid (10 Mar) [cal HYD-04], and before Holi (22 Mar) [cal HYD-05]. Fallback is 20-21 Mar if an SRH home IPL match lands on 13-14 Mar [cal HYD-09].

We do not split the crowd. Elan (9-11 Jan), Felicity (13-15 Feb) and Pearl/CBIT (about 19-22 Feb) are all over by March [fest HYD-01, fest HYD-04, fest HYD-07, fest HYD-11]. Free general entry is the local norm [fest HYD-03].

Scalable, permit-ready venue. HITEX Halls 1-3 seat 2,500 each and Hall-4 seats 8,000 theatre-style [cal HYD-16]. It is under Cyberabad police's online CPPMS permission system, which needs at least 10 days' notice for non-ticketed college events over 500 people [cal HYD-26], and is 2.6 km from HITEC City metro [cal HYD-15].
Peer-driven media fits loops. 70% of Indian Gen Z attend events in groups [MED-25]. Numaish's youth surge was linked to reels [fest HYD-16]. Hyderabad nano creators cost Rs 3-8k per reel [INF-03].

fest_dates_and_timeline.focus: Sponsor-funded venue LOI (HITEX) and production. Registration + QR + WhatsApp BSP stack, dedupe, 15% holdout randomiser. Dashboard and copilot pointed at the 2027 tables, with one campaign_id per bet. Shortlist 80 clubs, recruit 100 ambassadors, vet 10 creators, build a bank of 12 reels, get bus and booth quotes. Gate on 20 Dec: at least 15 MoUs in the pipeline and Meta templates approved.

Ambassador onboarding; 30 club MoUs by 3 Jan. Registrations and Squad Pass open Mon 4 Jan together with the line-up reveal. CTWA burst 1 runs as a CTWA vs landing-page split. Squad and league A/B tests start. Pause 13-17 Jan for the Sankranti holidays [fest HYD-21].

Club pre-events at 8 or more per week, CTWA burst 2, pop-ups on Sun 24 and Sun 31 Jan, 50 MoUs by 24 Jan. Gate on 31 Jan: A/B readouts, winning variants go to 100%, ambassadors with zero registrations are deactivated.
JNTUH II-IV mid-terms 1-6 Feb [cal HYD-01] and GATE 6-7 Feb [cal HYD-07]. Content only: no campus activations and no paid bursts.

Peak acquisition. The median gap from first contact to registration is 7 days [DS], so acquisition must peak at least 2 weeks before the fest. Ramadan runs from about 9 Feb [cal HYD-04], so pop-ups and messages go out after iftar. No activations on the GATE weekends of 13-14 and 20-21 Feb. CTWA bursts 3-4 with fresh creative. IPL fixture check by 15 Feb, which triggers the fallback-date decision. Plan-making prompts start 15 Feb. CPPMS application for a 5,000 peak filed by 20 Feb. Reserve released 21 Feb. Pacing gate on 1 Mar: at least 4,200 confirmed registrations unlocks the stretch pool.

T-7 reminder 6 Mar. Waitlist batches released 6, 9 and 12 Mar. First-years have mid-terms 3-9 Mar [cal HYD-02], so they are nudged only from 10 Mar. No messages on Eid (10 Mar); T-2 on the evening of 11 Mar; T-1 on 12 Mar. Bus manifests locked 11 Mar. Final 'bring one more' squad push.

QR + college-ID verified gate with 6 lanes, live occupancy against the 5,000 permission, walk-in lane capped at 300 a day. Morning-of reminder at 8 am. At 6 pm on day 1, verified attendees get a 'bring a friend tomorrow' link. The pro-nite in Hall-4 ends at 9:45 pm so shuttles reach HITEC City station before the 11 pm last metro [cal HYD-11, cal HYD-15].
Rewards paid only on verified check-ins. Holdout readout 15-17 Mar. Retro on cost per visitor and k for each bet. Event reels recap builds the 2028 seed audience.

base_case.arithmetic: Seeds: B1 Club Co-host 50 clubs x 24 = 1,200; B4 Ambassadors 100 x 60% active x 12 = 720; B5 Reels 450 CTWA + 200 creators + 350 organic = 1,000. Total seeds 2,920. framework.name: ICE (Impact, Confidence, Ease; Sean Ellis) [GRO-03], with Impact tied to modelled net verified visitors
framework.how_scored: Each factor is scored 1-10 and the score is (I+C+E)/3. Impact = base net verified visitors against the bet's 2025 channel analog: 400 or more = 9, 250-399 = 7, 150-249 = 6, 50-149 = 5, under 50 or negative = 3. Confidence = evidence tier: our own 2025 data on the same mechanic = 8; RCT or meta-analysis = 7-8; vendor benchmark only = 4-5; minus points where the key uplift rests on external data. Ease = 10 minus penalties: owner time over 8 hours a week = -2; cash over Rs 50k = -1; each external approval or dependency = -1. Results: B1 Club Co-host 7.7 and B2 Show-up Engine 7.7 (tie broken on impact); B3 Squad Pass 6.7; B4 Ambassador League 6.0; B5 Reels flywheel 4.7. Decision: double down on B1 and B2, the largest proven impact and the cheapest multiplier on every other bet. B3 is the growth spine but must earn the reserve by showing k of at least 0.20. B5 is cut to a seed-supply role.

ideas.name: B1 Club Co-host Quotas: 50 campus clubs bring members as verified batches
ideas.concept: Sign 50 partner clubs across the 3 metro engineering clusters and Osmania-area degree and women's colleges: IEEE student branches (132 in the Hyderabad Section [MED-18]), E-cells, NSS, and coding, dance and music clubs. Each club co-hosts one 60-90 minute on-campus qualifier or preview (a hackathon round, a BGMI lobby [fest HYD-17], a dance-off). In return it gets a batch registration code, a showcase slot or stall at the fest, and a free cluster bus on fest day once 40 members confirm. A weekly pipeline review with an idle alert prevents the 2025 stall.
ideas.why_it_works: This was the best 2025 channel on every quality metric: 90.0% identified-to-registered, 85.6% registered-to-visited, 4.0% cancellations, Rs 81 per visitor [DS]. Its limit was execution, not demand. Registrations went 21, 8, 0 in weeks 8-10 while spend postings skipped 4-28 Feb, then ran 64-97 a week once restarted (weeks 11-14) [DS]. A club batch is a ready-made squad (70% of Indian Gen Z attend in groups [MED-25]). Buses remove the distance penalty of 2-12pp per mile [SHOW-17] for peripheral colleges.
ideas.contribution_math: Base: 50 clubs x 24 = 1,200 registrations. The first 650 convert at the 2025 college + community rate of 84.6% (550 / 650 [DS]) = 550; the next 550 at 74.6% (A2 haircut) = 410.4. Total 960.4 visitors (80.0%). Net against the 2025 analog (385 college + 165 community = 550): +410. Stretch: 65 x 26 = 1,690 registrations, giving 550 + 1,040 x 74.6% = 1,326.0 visitors, net +776. Run-rate check: about 150 registrations a week over about 8 active weeks, at twice 2025's weekly spend, against 2025's about 80 a week once live. Sensitivity: plus or minus 10 clubs moves the total by plus or minus 234 visitors (including loop and show-up effects).
ideas.resources: Owner 2 (Partnerships lead), about 12 hours a week. 3 volunteer cluster captains (one per district, about 6 hours a week each). 50 club leads. Production supplies the showcase slots.
ideas.timeline: 26 Nov-20 Dec: shortlist and pitch 80 clubs. 30 MoUs by 3 Jan, 50 by 24 Jan. Pre-events 18-31 Jan and 8 Feb-5 Mar, with none during 1-7 Feb (mid-terms and GATE) and none on the 13-14 or 20-21 Feb GATE weekends; lunch slots during Ramadan. Bus quotas locked 6 Mar; buses run 13-14 Mar.
ideas.test_design: Stratified by cluster, randomise clubs to two pre-event formats: (A) competition qualifier, winners get a stage slot; (B) open workshop or preview. Primary metric: confirmed registrations per event; secondary: confirmation rate. Read on 14 Feb. Second test: half the clubs are offered the bus at 40 confirmed and half at 25; metric is cost per bus seat filled. With n = 50 clubs, decisions are directional (posterior comparison of means), not claims of significance.

ideas.name: B2 AI Show-up Engine: agentic WhatsApp ops that turn registrations into verified walk-ins
ideas.concept: One WhatsApp-first operations layer for every registrant: (1) dedupe on a stable ID plus fraud flags; (2) an instant QR pass worded as 'reserved for you' [SHOW-13]; (3) a plan-making prompt asking which day, which metro station or bus, and with whom [SHOW-14]; (4) squad check-in visibility [SHOW-15]; (5) a reminder cadence of T-7, T-2, T-1 and morning-of [SHOW-10], with no messages on Eid; (6) a loss-framed 'release your spot' message plus automatic waitlist batches and win-back of cancellations; (7) last-metro and shuttle details. A rules engine sends the messages. Gemini drafts copy variants and answers FAQs from the programme. A 15% randomised holdout gets the 2025 equivalent: QR pass plus one T-1 reminder.
ideas.why_it_works: Show-up is the cheapest lever. 2025 lost 875 of 2,800 registrants (31.2%), including 117 (4.2%) who leaked through the waitlist or never confirmed. The only nurture, a single email, gave zero lift (69.0% vs 68.7%) and a 12.7% opt-out [DS]. RCTs: reminders cut no-shows by 25% (RR 0.75) [SHOW-09]; two reminders beat one [SHOW-10]; ownership wording performed best [SHOW-13]; plan-making adds 4.1pp [SHOW-14]; social visibility adds 8.1pp [SHOW-15]. Leading indicators exist in our own data: programme download (74.7% vs 61.9% show-up) and asking a question (79.4% vs 68.0%) [DS]. Messages cost about Rs 0.25 all-in [WA-01] and are free for 7 days after a CTWA ad [WA-03].
ideas.contribution_math: The other bets produce 3,650 registrations and 2,604.0 visitors before B2 (71.3%), leaving 1,046.0 no-shows. Base: 20% fewer no-shows (more conservative than the 25% meta-analysis effect) x 85% treated = 177.8 visitors, lifting show-up from 71.3% to 76.2%. Stretch: 1,621.8 x 30% x 85% = 413.6, lifting show-up from 70.2% to 77.8%. Cost of proof: the holdout gives up 1,046 x 20% x 15% = 31 base visitors. Sensitivity: a 10% reduction gives -89 and a 30% reduction gives +89.
ideas.resources: Owner 1 (Growth lead, the candidate) builds the flows, dashboard and copilot: about 15 hours a week in December, then about 6. 1 volunteer handles template approvals and FAQs. 20 gate volunteers on event days for QR + college-ID checks.
ideas.timeline: 26 Nov-31 Dec: BSP onboarding, Meta template approval, dedupe, holdout randomiser, QR. 4 Jan: confirmations live. 15 Feb: plan-making prompt. 6, 9, 12 Mar: waitlist batches. Reminders 6 Mar (T-7), 11 Mar evening (T-2; skip Eid on 10 Mar), 12 Mar (T-1), 13 Mar 8 am. 13 Mar 9 pm: day-2 nudge. 15-17 Mar: holdout readout.
ideas.test_design: A 15% holdout, randomised at registrant level and stratified by bet, receives only the QR pass and T-1 reminder. With about 548 in the holdout and about 3,102 treated, the 95% CI on the lift is plus or minus 4.1pp, with about 79% power to detect the modelled 5.7pp lift (a 10% holdout would give only about 64%). Nested copy test inside the treatment group: T-1 ownership wording vs loss/release framing, about 1,550 per arm.

ideas.early_success_signal: By 15 Feb: at least 92% of registrants confirm within 72 hours, opt-out at or below 3%, at least 40% of those prompted complete a plan, and at least 60% download the programme.
ideas.early_failure_signal: Delivery below 90%; opt-out above 6%; confirmation rate below 88%; more than 15% replying 'can't come' at T-7.
ideas.scale_threshold: Opt-out at or below 3% and confirmation at or above 92%: add the squad-status nudge and a club-lead voice note at T-3, and extend the day-2 nudges to all day-1 attendees.
ideas.change_threshold: Opt-out between 3% and 6%: cut to 4 messages, move to utility-only templates, personalise by squad or club.
ideas.stop_threshold: Opt-out above 8% or complaints: stop all non-essential messages and keep only the QR pass, T-1 and morning-of. If the measured lift against the holdout is under 1pp, revert to the minimal cadence for 2028.
ideas.action_on_change: Weekly review on Thursday. The copilot proposes the next cadence or copy change and the waitlist release size, calculated as (cap - expected attendance) / waitlist show rate. Owner 1 approves before anything is sent.

Copilot: diagnose watches opt-out, cancellation and waitlist signals; calculate sizes waitlist releases exactly; create_task queues message changes behind human approval; it drafts copy variants and flags duplicate IDs.

ideas.name: B3 Squad Pass: a referral loop that pays only on verified group check-ins
ideas.concept: Registration ends with 'Who are you coming with?'. The registrant becomes a squad lead and gets a WhatsApp invite link for 2-5 friends. Perks unlock when at least 3 squad members check in (verified): fast-lane entry, front-zone pro-nite access, a squad reel at the photo booth. An inter-college Squad Cup ranks colleges by verified check-ins per 100 registrants. At 6 pm on day 1, verified attendees get a 'bring one friend tomorrow' link (2025 had 620 day-2-only visitors [DS]). All rewards are non-cash and paid only after verification, so fake sign-ups earn nothing.
ideas.why_it_works: Referrals were the cheapest 2025 channel (Rs 69 per visitor, 78.6% show-up, 4.8% CTR) but produced only 12.5% of registrations, an implied k of 0.125 [DS]. Squads match how people attend: 70% of Indian Gen Z go to events in groups [MED-25], and 59% would skip an event if they knew no one [SHOW-16]. Festival referral programmes add 20-30% to sales, and Camp Bestival got 30% of pre-sale sign-ups through referrals [REF-02]. The loop turns every registrant from every other bet into a seed.
ideas.contribution_math: k = share rate x invites x invite-to-registration rate. Base: 0.22 x 3 x 0.30 = 0.198, rounded to 0.20 (A3). Stretch: 0.25 x 3 x 0.333 = 0.25. Extole's generic 0.19 x 2 x 0.13 = 0.049 [REF-01] is a floor that 2025 already beat. B3 registrations = seeds x k / (1 - k): base 2,920 x 0.25 = 730. The first 350 convert at 78.6% = 275, the next 380 at 68.6% = 260.6, for 535.6 visitors, net +261 against 2025's 275. Stretch: 4,082 x 0.333 = 1,360.7 registrations, giving 275 + 1,010.7 x 68.6% = 968.0, net +693. Sensitivity on the total: k = 0.15 gives -159; k = 0.25 at base seeds gives +180.
ideas.resources: Owner 3 (Community lead) runs rewards and the Squad Cup, about 5 hours a week. Owner 1 builds the squad data model into the registration flow, shared with B2. 2 volunteers staff the booth on event days.
ideas.timeline: Build 1-20 Dec. Launch with registrations on 4 Jan. A/B runs 4-31 Jan, read on 31 Jan. Scale 8 Feb-12 Mar. Day-1-to-day-2 link at 6 pm on 13 Mar. Rewards paid 15-20 Mar after verification.
ideas.test_design: Registrant-level A/B from 4 Jan. Arm A: a standard individual referral link, rewarded when the friend's check-in is verified. Arm B: Squad Pass, with a group unlock at 3 verified members. Primary metrics: share rate and k. About 480 registrants per arm detects a move in share rate from 15% to 22% at 80% power and alpha 0.05. Read on 31 Jan; the winner goes to 100%. Follow-up test: unlock at 3 vs 4 members.

ideas.name: B4 Ambassador League: 100 campus ambassadors ranked on verified check-ins, not sign-ups
ideas.concept: Recruit 100 ambassadors: one per target college, two in each of the 20 largest, including women's and Osmania-area degree colleges. A weekly league table ranks them on confirmed registrations before the event and pays out on verified check-ins after it. Non-cash tiers: certificate at 10 verified visitors, T-shirt at 25, pro-nite VIP pass and recommendation letter for the top 20, internship interviews with GCC sponsors for the top 10 (515 GCCs in Hyderabad [mkt HYD-26]). Cluster captains, one per 10 ambassadors, run weekly challenges.
ideas.why_it_works: In 2025 ambassadors delivered 19.0% of visitors (390) for 15.3% of spend, at Rs 108 per visitor and 75% show-up [DS]. Rewards based on sign-ups invite low-intent registrations; paying on verified check-ins aligns ambassadors with the North Star. National fests scale on tiered, almost cash-free rewards: Techfest gives free accommodation to its top 10 and recommendation letters to its top 100 [NAT-05]; IIT Ropar gives a free pass at 100+ registrations [CA-01]; Vignan sets a 50-registration minimum [CA-02].
ideas.contribution_math: Base: 100 recruited x 60% active x 12 = 720 registrations. The first 520 convert at the 2025 ambassador rate of 75% = 390, the next 200 at 65% = 130, for 520.0 visitors (72.2%), net +130 against 2025's 390. Stretch: 120 x 65% x 14 = 1,092 registrations, giving 390 + 572 x 65% = 761.8, net +372. Twelve registrations per active ambassador sits at the bottom of IIT Ropar's 10-40 certificate tier. Sensitivity: plus or minus 10pp in the active share moves the total by plus or minus 107.
ideas.resources: Owner 3 (Community lead), about 8 hours a week, plus 10 cluster captains promoted from the top ambassadors. Free listing on Unstop or Internshala [SHOW-28]. A 30-minute league call each week.
ideas.timeline: Recruit 1-20 Dec. Onboarding kit and personal links 21 Dec-3 Jan. League weeks run 4 Jan-7 Mar, paused 13-17 Jan (Sankranti) and 1-7 Feb (mid-terms). Final push 8-12 Mar. Payout 15-20 Mar after verification.
ideas.test_design: Stratified by college size, randomise ambassadors into a solo leaderboard or a captain-led cluster team league with team rewards for weeks 1-4. Primary metrics: share of ambassadors active, and confirmed registrations per ambassador per week. Read on 31 Jan and adopt the winner.

ideas.name: B5 Reels-to-WhatsApp flywheel: geo-fenced Click-to-WhatsApp Reels, Telugu nano creators and filmed pop-ups
ideas.concept: Replace 2025's feed ads and creator posts, which took 55.4% of spend for 25.1% of visitors [DS], with four pieces. (a) Click-to-WhatsApp (CTWA) Reels ads geo-fenced to the 3 engineering districts, run as 4 two-week bursts with fresh creative each burst. (b) 8-10 Hyderabad Telugu nano and micro creators, screened for engagement of 3% or more and authentic audiences [INF-03, INF-04], half of them female-led. (c) 4 filmed pop-ups at youth hubs such as malls and metro stations (Felicity's mall flashmob drew 750+ [fest HYD-05]), held after iftar during Ramadan. (d) Event-day reels that feed day-2 visits and the 2028 audience. Everything lands in the WhatsApp registration bot, so every B5 registrant becomes a squad lead (B3) and enters B2's cadence.
ideas.why_it_works: Loops need seeds: B5 supplies 1,000 of the 2,920 seed registrations (34%) and city-wide awareness that peer channels cannot reach. Reels CPM is Rs 45-140, against Rs 150-350 for feed [PAID-01]. CTWA skips the landing page, where only 21.7% of 2025 paid-social sessions started a registration [DS], and opens a free 7-day messaging window [WA-03]. February-March is a cheap window for Meta CPMs [PAID-03]. Refreshing creative each burst addresses the 2025 collapse, when registrations fell from 105 to 35 a week at a flat Rs 14,400 a week [DS].
ideas.contribution_math: Base registrations: CTWA Rs 50,000 / Rs 111 per registration (19% better than 2025 paid social's Rs 137) = 450; creators Rs 35,000 / Rs 175 per registration (about 2025's Rs 169) = 200; organic, city pages and pop-ups 350 (2025 organic 250 + 4 pop-ups x 25). Visitors: 450 x 50% + 200 x 50% + 250 x 78% + 100 x 68% = 588.0. Net against the 2025 analog (340 paid + 175 creators + 195 organic = 710) is -122, and that is deliberate. B5's cash falls from Rs 1,66,000 to Rs 1,00,000, and the Rs 66,000 saved buys visitors in B1-B4 at Rs 56-141 each instead of B5's Rs 170. Its 1,000 seeds also generate 250 squad registrations, which are credited to B3. Cross-check: Rs 50k at Rs 100 CPM, 2.1% CTR and 9.9% click-to-registration (2025 paid) would give about 1,040 registrations, so 450 is conservative. At 2025's Rs 137 per registration we would get 365, costing 65 visitors. Stretch: 550 + 250 + 500 registrations give 275 + 125 + 365 = 765.0 visitors, net +55.
ideas.resources: Owner 4 (Content lead), about 10 hours a week, plus 6 content volunteers who shoot and edit, and the creators. Owner 1 sets up the geo-fence and CTWA tracking codes.
ideas.timeline: December: bank of 12 reels and creator vetting. Burst 1: 4-12 Jan, timed with the line-up reveal. Burst 2: 18-31 Jan. Burst 3: 8-21 Feb. Burst 4: 22 Feb-7 Mar. Pop-ups on Sun 24 Jan, Sun 31 Jan, Sat 27 Feb and Sun 7 Mar (avoiding the GATE weekends and Shivaratri on 6 Mar). Event reels 13-14 Mar.
ideas.test_design: Burst 1 splits the budget 50/50 between CTWA and landing-page ads with the same creative, about Rs 6k per arm. The metric is cost per confirmed registration, not cost per click. Each creator gets a unique code and is ranked on cost per confirmed registration. For one burst, compare a geo-fence on the engineering districts against city-wide 18-24 targeting.

drafts.overlap_adjustment: Five rules prevent double counting. (1) One person = one stable ID (phone + college-ID hash), deduped before counting. Only external people with an admitted + verified QR check-in count, as in the 2025 rules [DS]. (2) Each registration carries exactly one source code: the first-touch code at identification, the same attribution rule as the 2025 dataset. A squad link from a non-ambassador peer counts to B3; an ambassador link, including squads an ambassador starts, counts to B4; a club batch code counts to B1; a CTWA ad, creator code, UTM or organic visit counts to B5; registration at the gate counts as a walk-in. (3) The loop is modelled once: B3 = seeds x k/(1-k), so B1, B4 and B5 contain no referred registrations. (4) Each bet's visitors use its pre-B2 show rate. B2 claims only the extra visitors above that, on the 85% treated, measured against the 15% holdout. (5) Scale haircut: registrations above each channel's 2025 volume show up at a rate 10pp lower, so scaled volume is never credited at the best historical rate. Base check: B3 535.6 + B1 960.4 + B4 520.0 + B2 177.8 + B5 588.0 + walk-ins 150 = 2,931.8. Net against 2025: +260.6 + 410.4 + 130.0 + 177.8 - 122.0 + 25 = +881.8 = 2,931.8 - 2,050. Stretch: 968.0 + 1,326.0 + 761.8 + 413.6 + 765.0 + 250 = 4,484.4. Net: +693.0 + 776.0 + 371.8 + 413.6 + 55.0 + 125 = +2,434.4 = 4,484.4 - 2,050. The per-idea integers are rounded from these figures.
