headline_numbers: Base: 2,932 unique verified external visitors (+43% on 2025's 2,050) on Rs 3,00,000, at Rs 102 per verified visitor (2025: Rs 134)
Stretch: 4,484 (2.2x 2025) on Rs 3,30,000, at Rs 74 per visitor; the extra Rs 30k unlocks only after 4,200 confirmed registrations by 1 Mar
Registrant show-up: 68.8% in 2025 to 76.2% base and 77.8% stretch; channel mix alone gives 71.3%
Squad loop k: 0.125 (2025 implied) to 0.20 base and 0.25 stretch; 730 and 1,361 squad registrations
Paid social + creators fall from 55.4% of spend to 28.3% (Rs 85k); peer bets bring 73% of base registrations
Base is 0.37% of the about 8 lakh Hyderabad + Ranga Reddy students: conversion, not reach, is the constraint
Stretch pro-nite peak of 3,253 people against a 5,000 permission (65%); hard cap of 6,500 registrations
Proof: a 15% holdout costs about 31 visitors and gives about 79% power on the show-up lift

math_errors: The x1.10 stall fix on the grid is partly double counted. In 2025 the stall weeks (7, 8 and 10) had zero partnership spend posted, so the 2025 cost per registration already reflects the gap, and scaling spend from Rs 31K to Rs 80K already recovers that volume. Removing the fix lowers base by about 65 visitors, which the draft's own sensitivity line confirms.

The holdout's minimum detectable effect of 5.2 pp (about 510 vs 2,890, one-sided) ignores the design effect of randomising at squad level, so the real MDE is larger. The modelled treated-vs-holdout gap is about 5 pp, so the test is closer to 50-60% power than 80%.

The line 'the same Rs 92K buys ~680 visitors at the grid's Rs 135 marginal CPV' is rhetorical. The grid is capped by team bandwidth at 40 partners and absorbs only +Rs 49K, so the Rs 92K cannot all buy grid visitors.
Minor: the 93% confirm rate is presentation-only (the draft admits this). 'February is the cheapest CPM month' rests on a single year's data point [PAID-03].
best_elements_to_keep: An exact additive decomposition. Acquisition ideas get (R1-R0) x s0, the show-up engine gets R1 x (s1-s0), and the paid/creator/organic shrink is booked as an explicit -242 line. The waterfall 2,050-242+382+142+71+48+203+150 = 2,804 reconciles exactly (verified).

Paid beta 0.62 derived from 2025's own weekly data (verified): the first Rs 52.8K bought 479 registrations at Rs 110 each and the last Rs 40.2K bought 201 at Rs 200 each. This is the strongest single evidence point in any draft.
The partnership stall measured from the data (verified): 29 registrations in weeks 8-10 against 78 at the weeks 6-7 run-rate, so 49 were lost.

A projected-CPV gate on every idea: Rs 120 or less = scale; Rs 120-200 = hold; Rs 200-250 = change; above Rs 250 for 2 weeks = stop. Plus a Rs 30K reserve released on 8 Feb only to the lowest measured marginal CPV, and only if that is Rs 200 or less.
Honest about the competition track's full cost: Rs 74 per visitor in cash but about Rs 1,305 with sponsor prizes, cut if no sponsor signs by 15 Jan.
Hard capacity caps (4,500 passes, 300 walk-ins a day, a 7,000 CPPMS permit, worst case 6,300), plus a downside floor of 2,158 that still beats 2025.

The best calendar detail of any draft: reconfirm moved off Shivaratri (6 Mar), T-2 after Eid, first-years messaged only after their 9 Mar mid-terms, competition prelims on weekdays because GATE takes the weekends.
Base keeps referral yield near 2025 (15.4 vs 14.3 per 100 registrants), so it does not lean on an untested squad uplift.
fatal_flaws: None fatal. The weak spot is creativity: the five ideas are the standard set, and #4 ('paid rebuild') shrinks and fixes an existing channel rather than placing a new bet. A reviewer may say it fills a slot.

math_errors: The overlap deduction cannot be traced. The draft says 25% of squad-link registrations (199 registrations, 156 visitors) were removed as already coded, but k = 0.35 x 3 x 0.17 = 0.1785 contains no 0.75 factor. The claimed '316 double-claimed visitors removed' cannot be reproduced from the arithmetic shown.

The triangulation is not independent. The cross-checks (3,245 and 3,028) apply 2025 average peer CPV (Rs 88.9) linearly to 2.4x the peer spend, which assumes no diminishing returns, the very effect the draft documents for paid. So 'within 9%' confirms nothing.

Implied unit costs beat 2025's best channels at much higher volume: clubs about Rs 62.5 per registration (2025 partner+community Rs 72), ambassadors about Rs 57 (2025 Rs 81), squads about Rs 32 (2025 referrals Rs 54).
The club show rate stays at 80% across 1,600 registrations, only 4.6 pp below the 2025 blend of 84.6% on 650. Other drafts haircut incremental volume by 10 pp.

The stretch claim of 'marginal Rs 18 per extra visitor' (Rs 30K / 1,661) credits cash for gains that come from assumptions (44 vs 32 clubs, k 0.204, +6 pp show-up). It also ignores that the base's uncredited Rs 30K reserve gets spent, so the real extra cash is Rs 60K.
best_elements_to_keep: The club as the distribution unit: batch codes, in-kind payment (stage slots, competition tracks), and a Club Cup ranked on verified attendees. It is a sharper version of 'college partnerships'.
Charters sequenced cluster by cluster along metro corridors (Kukatpally-Bachupally-Miyapur and Gandipet-Gachibowli first), with a stall detector that alerts after 7 days of zero registrations.
Show-up capped against an external benchmark: blended registered-to-visited held at or below 82% [SHOW-02].
The permit filed under the 14-day ticketed rule, so a Rs 99 refundable test cell cannot change the approver.
A 2x2 factorial for wording x plan-making, with a correct MDE (about 3.9 pp), plus a geo holdout read with difference-in-differences for media.
Useful deprioritisations: Inter students (exams 24 Feb-20 Mar), the OU Arts College event ban, mall flashmobs as reach without a registration path.
fatal_flaws: The base case behaves like a stretch. 3,288 (+60%) rests on unsourced per-unit yields: 20 registrations per club x 2.5 clubs x 32 active colleges, 15 per ambassador, and k 0.18. The draft itself admits the 2025 data has no college field to backtest per-club yield. This is the 'big number without evidence' that RISA reviewers penalise.

Registration opens 8 Feb, so about 3,950 registrations must land in roughly 26 days that include two GATE weekends and Ramadan. That is about 1,000 a week, against a 2025 peak of about 354 a week. The 15 Feb 'master checkpoint' falls 7 days after opening, and the pilot gate ('registrations per club by day 10' from 3 Jan) is measured before registration exists.

math_errors: Squad k in the base is 0.296, about 2.1x 2025's 0.14, and it is the plan's most sensitive input (-288 if squad start rate is 10%). At 764 registrations for Rs 35K, squads also exceed the plan's own marginal-CPR rule: about 587 at 1.25x CPR above the 2025 referral spend.
Registrant show-up of 81.0% (base) and 86.5% (stretch) sits at or above PheedLoop's median for large PAID events (82% [SHOW-02]) for a free fest. The ceiling is never acknowledged.
The bus step uses a 14.3% residual no-show, but the sequential residual at that point is about 13.8%. Trivial in size.
The segment size of about 2.9 lakh uses 675 x 4 with no occupancy adjustment, despite 79-91% fill [HYD-10]. It is not load-bearing.

The holdout's MDE (about 5 pp with n of about 470) is above the modelled effect (about 3.8 pp). The draft says so honestly and pre-registers a directional read, but the engine's +102 cannot be confirmed statistically.
best_elements_to_keep: Conversion levers applied sequentially to the residual no-shows, in a declared order: leak-proof, then engine, then squad visibility, then ladder, then bus. The standalone sum (261) is shown against the sequential sum (249), so the overlap removed is explicit. Waterfall 2,050-298+102+553+310+77+38 = 2,832 verified.
Growth decomposed into more registrations (+373) and better show-up (+409, 52%). This fits Challenge A's 'actually attend' framing.

Leak-proof capacity: auto-confirm, overbooking each zone by capacity / forecast show rate [SHOW-21], waitlist batches, and a cancel flow offering switch day / transfer / release. It is built on exact 2025 counts: 300 of 875 no-shows never held a live pass.

The commitment ladder as a randomised encouragement design. It tests whether the brochure (74.7% vs 61.9%) and question (79.4% vs 68.0%) correlations are causal, and the copilot keeps correlation and causation separate.
One comparison: Rs 20K of conversion work (217 visitors at Rs 92 each) against the Rs 55K left in paid (the same 217 at Rs 254 each).
A matched-pair staggered wave rollout to measure the causal lift from partnering, and a partner-bus pilot to measure the distance penalty the data lacks.

Four dated gates (18 Jan, 8 Feb, 22 Feb, 6 Mar) with pacing targets of 15/40/65/92% of registrations, and a 75 person-week team budget split across ideas. This is the best proof the plan fits 5 owners.
A money hurdle: any idea asking for incremental cash must beat the partners' marginal cost of Rs 128 per visitor.
fatal_flaws: None fatal. The risk is distinctness: ideas #1, #4 and #5 all run on the same WhatsApp show-up rail, and #4 and #5 add only 77 and 38 visitors. A reviewer may say the 'five strategies' are one show-up system split three ways, plus #2, which bundles partners, ambassadors, clubs and buses.

math_errors: The stretch claim of 'marginal Rs 19.3 per extra visitor' (Rs 30K / 1,552.6) credits cash for gains that come from assumptions: k 0.25, 65 clubs x 26, 120 ambassadors and a headliner.
B5 keeps 250 organic registrations with no organic budget line. 2025 spent Rs 14K on organic, and the B5 money goes to CTWA, creators and pop-ups.

B1 economics: of Rs 75K, Rs 40K goes on buses (a show-up cost), so Rs 35K of kits buys 1,200 registrations. That is about Rs 29 per registration, against Rs 69 for 2025 partnerships and Rs 80 for community. B4 (720 registrations on Rs 40K, about Rs 56 against Rs 81) is also optimistic.
The reach back-solve (2.68 lakh) applies the paid-style CTR x impressions path to peer and club registrations. It is labelled non-load-bearing, so this is a nit.
best_elements_to_keep: A clean loop model. B3 = seeds x k / (1-k), modelled once, so the seed bets contain no referred registrations. Diagnosing k as share x invites x conversion turns it into a usable leading indicator. Base arithmetic 2,931.8 verified.
A day-1 6 pm 'bring a friend tomorrow' link aimed at the 2025 pattern of 620 day-2-only visitors. It is creative and grounded in the data.
The most conservative show-up in any draft: 71.3% from channel mix, rising to 76.2% with the engine, in line with the 76% median for large free events [SHOW-02].
A worked power calculation for the 15% holdout (about 79% power at 5.7 pp; 10% would give only 64%) and a squad A/B sample size (about 480 per arm for 15% to 22%). Both are verified.
Ambassador league rewards include GCC internship interviews for the top 10: a non-cash reward that is valuable in Hyderabad.
A registration hard cap of 6,500, with a worked worst-case peak of 4,320 against a 5,000 permit, and HICC as the fallback venue.
A citation key that disambiguates fact IDs repeated across brief sections.
fatal_flaws: The budget contradicts the ranking. The rank-5 bet (B5), with a negative net contribution (-122) and the worst cost per visitor (Rs 170), gets the largest line: Rs 1,00,000, 33% of cash. 'Double down' B2 gets Rs 25K. 'Loops need seeds' does not justify this, because B1 and B4 seeds are cheaper. A reviewer grading deliberate trade-offs will catch it at once.

verdicts.recommended_targets:
BASE: about 2,800 unique verified external visitors (range 2,750-2,850) on Rs 3,00,000. That is +37-38% on 2,050 at about Rs 106-107 per verified visitor, against Rs 134 in 2025. STRETCH: about 3,450-3,530 on the same Rs 3,00,000 (+68-72%, Rs 85-87 per visitor). FLOOR: about 2,150-2,400, still above 2025.

Why these numbers are credible:
(1) Two independent methods converge. The unit-economics draft uses channel response curves with a measured paid beta and a measured stall fix and gets 2,804. The show-up draft uses a CPR step function and sequential no-show attribution and gets 2,832. They are within 1% of each other.
(2) Both keep 2025 channel show rates as priors, haircut scaled volume, and keep paid and creators at 50% show.
(3) The registrant show rate rises from 68.8% to about 79-81%. That sits at or under PheedLoop's 76-82% benchmarks for large free and paid events, and the 2025 partner channel already reached 85.6% with no reminders.
(4) The base is about 0.5% of the priority pool, so it does not depend on reach.

Why I reject the larger stretches: 4,484 (loops) and 4,949 (community) both need extra cash, assume unit costs fall as spend rises, rely on geometric referral loops at k 0.20-0.25, and (in loops) a sponsor headliner. Both attribute the whole stretch uplift to the extra Rs 30K, at 'Rs 18-19 per extra visitor'. Skeptical reviewers will discount all of it.

If a bigger number is wanted, present it as a funded option, not a target: beyond the stretch, each extra Rs 10K buys about 70 visitors at Rs 135-150 marginal CPV, released only after the 8 Feb readout proves that rate.

Capacity is not binding in any case. File CPPMS for about 5,000 with a pass cap of about 4,500-6,500 and a 300-a-day walk-in cap.
synthesis_advice: Scoring method: total = 0.20 ambition_quant + 0.20 evidence_rigor + 0.10 creativity + 0.20 prioritisation + 0.15 experimentation + 0.15 Hyderabad feasibility, which mirrors the slide weights plus an operator-feasibility check. The deciding factor was evidence_rigor, because RISA penalises projections.

SLIDE 1 spine: use the unit-economics response-curve funnel and its exact waterfall (2,050 - 242 + idea increments = 2,804). Add the show-up draft's decomposition line: about half of the growth comes from people who already registered (show rate 68.8% to about 79-81%). Cite the convergence of 2,804 and 2,832 as the confidence argument, and show the downside floor.

Fix small fact slips before the slides go out. Identified-to-registered is 2,800 / 3,500 = 80.0%, not 77.2%, because walk-ins sit in the 3,625. Adjust segment sizes for 79-91% seat fill. State the 2025 k as 0.143 referrals per non-referral registrant, and if the k/(1-k) form is used, explain that it gives 0.125.

SLIDE 2, five distinct ranked bets. (1) College partnership grid / club charters, sequenced along the community draft's metro corridors and run on the unit-economics response curve, beta 0.75 and 20% haircut. (2) A 'reserved-for-you' show-up engine that absorbs the leak-proof capacity rules (auto-confirm, T-7/T-3/T-1 waitlist batches, switch-day or transfer instead of cancel, zone overbooking), with the commitment ladder and the Rs 99 deposit as test cells inside it rather than separate bets. (3) A verified-check-in peer loop (squad pass plus ambassador ladder) with the loops draft's day-1 6 pm 'bring a friend tomorrow' link. (4) Paid rebuilt as Click-to-WhatsApp Reels plus Telugu nano creators behind a CPV kill switch, cut from Rs 1.52L to about Rs 55-60K. (5) A sponsor-gated compete-to-attend track with a 15 Jan go/no-go.

Rank the largest proven lever (the grid) first and the engine second. Never put a bet with negative net contribution in the top five: present 'shrink paid' as the deprioritisation line with its explicit negative (-242 / -298) and the Rs 564-saved-per-visitor-given-up trade-off.

Overlap: combine the unit-economics single-source precedence (competition code, then partner, then squad/referral, then ambassador, then paid/creator, then organic) and its 20%/40% haircuts with the show-up draft's fixed order for conversion effects (leak recovery, engine, squad visibility, ladder, bus). State the number of double-counted visitors removed.

Feasibility proof: carry over the show-up draft's person-week budget (about 75 person-weeks across 5 owners and 15 weeks) and size the grid to fit it, about 35-40 partners. Drop to 45-60 ambassadors, only in non-partner colleges. Replace the 24-hour overnight hackathon with a 10-12 hour daytime one, which avoids overnight venue hire, police permission and security.

Registration window: open Mon 18 Jan (the unit-economics choice). Not 8 Feb, which compresses about 3,900 registrations into 4 weeks at about 3x the 2025 peak run-rate, and not 4 Jan, which adds early drift and the Sankranti dead week. Add a T-30 reconfirm for anyone registered more than 30 days out. Acquisition must peak by about 27 Feb given the 7-day median lag.

Hyderabad operator corrections the drafts missed. (a) Buses: most private engineering students are day scholars who live across the city, so run pickups along existing college-bus city routes ending at HITEX rather than from the campus. After the Aug 2026 Malla Reddy police cases, expect managements to demand parental consent and liability cover, so budget time for that. (b) Women students' night travel and parental curfews: end the pro-nite at 9:45 pm and offer women-priority bus and shuttle seats. Message route and last-train plans in plan-making. (c) Check each partner's autonomous-college calendar (several large JNTUH-affiliated colleges set their own mid-terms). (d) 13 Mar is a second Saturday, often a college holiday, which is a plus to verify per college. (e) The IPL fixture check on SRH home matches at Uppal triggers the 20-21 Mar fallback.

Permissions: file Cyberabad CPPMS for about 5,000 (not 7,000) at least 4-6 weeks out, under the 14-day ticketed route if any refundable pass test runs. Hard-cap passes and walk-ins, and show the worst case staying under the permit. Venue, production, prizes and the shuttle loop are explicitly sponsor-funded and out of scope, and if the shuttle is not sponsored it comes from the reserve.

SLIDE 3: keep the unit-economics shared projected-CPV gate (Rs 120 or less scale, Rs 120-200 hold, Rs 200-250 change, above Rs 250 for 2 weeks stop) as the common rule. Add per-idea leading indicators: partner registrations per week with a 7-day dark-partner alert, the T-8 reconfirm gap between treated and holdout, squad share rate and k, the paid CTR-decay fatigue alert and geo-lift, and competition slot fill at 15 Jan and 14 Feb.

Experiments to keep: a 15% squad-level holdout with the MDE stated honestly (about 5 pp, roughly equal to the base effect). Also the staggered Wave A/B partner rollout, the community draft's 2x2 factorial on reminder wording x plan-making, the CTWA geo-lift holdout, the squad vs plain-link A/B, and the encouragement design for brochure and question nudges.

Dashboard and copilot: every reallocation, send or disqualification needs human approval, and only aggregated non-PII data reaches the free-tier model. The copilot says when a sample is too small to call a result, and it recalibrates the show priors from reconfirm rates after T-8.

Language discipline for RISA reviewers: label every number as either a fact (with its ID) or an assumption (with its basis and sensitivity). Remove any 'marginal Rs 18-19 per stretch visitor' claim. Do not assume unit costs fall as spend grows. Keep a headliner out of the base and the stretch.
